               347.00        COMMUNITY POLICING STRATEGIES

347.01 POLICE AND COMMUNITY RELATIONSHIPS
Citizen participation and interaction with the police are necessary to promote cooperative efforts
in resolving community issues. It is shared responsibility of all Department members to
establish and promote rapport with members of the community. The Department must strive for
the establishment of a climate where officers may perform their duties with the acceptance,
understanding, and approval of the public. Additionally, the willing and practiced participation
of the people in enforcing the law is essential for the preservation of freedom.
A. Community policing is a philosophy that promotes organizational strategies that support the
    systemic use of partnerships and problem-solving techniques to proactively address the
    immediate conditions that give rise to public safety issues such as crime, social disorder,
    and fear of crime.
B. A reverence and respect for the dignity of all persons and the sanctity of all human life shall
    guide all training and leadership. Members of law enforcement derive their authority from
    the public; and therefore, must be ever mindful that they are not only the guardians, but also
    the servants of the public. Just as all persons are subject to the law, all persons have a right
    to dignified treatment under the law, and the protection of this right is a duty, which is as
    binding on the Department as any other.
C. All officers must treat a person with as much respect as that person will allow, and officers
    must be constantly mindful that the people with whom deal with each day are individuals with
    human emotions and needs. Such conduct is not a duty imposed in addition to an officer's
    primary responsibilities; it is inherent in them.
D. In dealing with all people, each officer must attempt to make their contact one which inspires
    respect as an individual and professional, and one which generates the cooperation and
    approval of the public. While entitled to personal beliefs, an officer cannot allow individual
    feelings or prejudices to enter into public contacts. However, since an officer's prejudices
    may be subconsciously manifested, it is incumbent upon the officer to strive to avoid the
    influence of attitudes which might impair impartiality and effectiveness, keeping in mind that
    initial contacts leave lasting impressions both of the individual officer and of the Department
    as a whole.
E. To ensure equal treatment in similar circumstances, all officers must be alert to situations
    where, because of a language barrier or for some other reason, officers may be called upon to
    display additional patience and understanding in dealing with what might otherwise appear to
    be a lack of response.
F. The Department must be responsive to the needs and problems of the community. While the
    Department's task is governed by the law, the policies formulated to guide the enforcement of
    the law must include consideration of the public will. This responsiveness must be manifested
    at all levels of the Department by a willingness to listen and by a genuine concern for the
    problems of individuals or groups. The total needs of the community must become an integral
    part of the programs designed to carry out the mission of the Department.
G. To promote understanding and cooperation, there must be interpersonal communication
    between members of the community and officers at all levels of the Department. All
    employees must be aware of the law enforcement needs of the community and their particular
    assigned area of responsibility. Guided by policy, an officer must tailor their performance to
    attain the objective of the Department and to solve the specific crime problems in the area the
                                           246
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


   officer serves. The Department must provide for programs to encourage productive dialogue
   with the public at all levels and to ensure that the unity of the police and the public is
   preserved.
H. It is necessary that there be full public disclosure of policies and openness in matters of public
   interest. Consistent with protection of legal rights of involved individuals and with
   consideration of the necessity for maintenance and confidentiality of Department records and
   of other primary Department responsibilities, the Department is to disseminate accurate and
   factual accounts of occurrences of public interest. Additionally, the Department must strive
   to make known and accepted its objectives and policies.
I. It is the duty of every employee of the Department to build an open relationship and dialog
   with the community served. This is accomplished through a variety of means to include, but
   not limited to, community forums and meetings, open house, citizen advisory committees, and
   specifically-targeted programs. The Department seeks to develop partnerships and resources
   within the community to build problem-solving groups and to instill a sense of mutual
   responsibility toward enhancing public safety and to increase the community’s ability to
   resolve issues related to crime or a perception of crime. The following areas should be
   considered when employees are working with community members:
    1. Exchange of helpful information.
    2. Promote police services that are available to the community.
    3. Discuss Department objectives, community problems, and successes.
    4. Encourage discussion to promote action aimed at solving problems that may exist.
    5. Educate citizens about the functions and operations of the Department.
    6. Obtain input from community groups to ensure that Department community relation
         policies and/or training reflect the needs of the community.
    7. Identify sources of conflict between the Department and the community and encourage
         efforts to resolve them.
J. Command staff, with input of all employees and the community, shall conduct evaluations at
   least twice a year regarding Department community relation plans and programs, analyzing the
   methods that have been effective and substituting poorly performing programs and/or methods
   of action with new approaches. Command staff shall also outline the Department’s
   expectations of community trust building for all officers and non-sworn employees setting out
   measurable objectives expected from the specific units and/or programs.
   1. Input on community relations plans and programs from the community should be sought
        through community forums, informal meetings such as Coffee with a Cop, and Code Blue
        representatives.
   2. Input from the employees on community relations plans and programs should be sought by
        command staff through specific email addresses, employee meetings, after action reports,
        and direct contact with program coordinators.
K. Specialized Units and Department Programs directed to the Community.
   Each unit and/or program shall outline in their Standard Operating Procedures the specifics of
   measurable objectives, evaluations and their level of review, necessary training, expectations
   of the employee, and the content and schedule of reports and meetings. Standard Operating
   Procedures shall be reviewed annually and approved by the appropriate deputy chief.
    1. Neighborhood Police Officer (NPO) - Foremost in the duties of the Neighborhood Police
         Officer is the responsibility of promoting the concept of community policing through
         working in the neighborhoods, housing communities, recreational centers, businesses, and
         other community entities by providing a direct link between the community and the police.
                                            247
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


        Neighborhood Police Officers work together with the community to identify and resolve
        problems that have caused or might cause discord between them. Improving police
        community relations is re-enforced by:
       a. Taking every opportunity to talk to and with the public,
       b. Being visible to the community and neighborhood,
       c. Taking part in the life of the community by joining civic, church, or private
           organizations,
       d. Becoming knowledgeable of services available to individuals and groups, and
       e. Becoming an active volunteer.
       f. Providing a weekly report, forwarded through their chain of command to the Chief of
           Police and City Council, detailing the officer’s interaction and communication with
           community members.
    2. Public Information Programs – As part of the community relations plans, the Public
        Relations Team publicize Department objectives, problems, and successes through
        departmental reports and social media.
    3. Crime Prevention Programs – Provide citizen groups with information on making their
        families, homes, and businesses more secure and work to establish crime watch
        neighborhoods where none exist. Employees assigned to crime prevention programs shall
        maintain monthly reports on measurable objectives of their program. Employees shall
        conduct safety fairs, communicate directly with their community for updated information
        and programs, and provide presentations.
    4. Community Volunteer Programs – Officers are assigned or volunteer to coordinate and
        work with specific groups and programs which involve community members. Officers
        provide training, on-going and up-to-date information, meetings, and serve as the direct
        link between the Department and the community individuals participating in various
        different programs such as the Citizens on Patrol Program (both English speaking and
        Spanish speaking), Code Blue in the Schools, Citizen Police Academy (both English
        speaking and Spanish speaking), Citizen Police Academy Alumni Program, Police-Clergy
        Programs, and Community Emergency Response Teams. Employees assigned to
        community volunteer programs shall maintain monthly reports on measurable objectives
        of their program(s).
    5. Advisory Boards
         a. Chief’s Advisory Board - The goal of the Chief's Advisory Board is to provide a
             forum for police-community interaction to address public safety and related issues in
             order to further enhance the quality of life in our community and is comprised of a
             diverse cross-section of community leaders representative of the City of Fort Worth.
         b. Policy Advisory Board - The primary purpose of the Policy Advisory Committee is
             to convene a forum of key leaders/stakeholders from diverse cross-sections of the
             community representative of the City of Fort Worth, and introduce them to the
             policies the Department has developed based on legislation, court cases, training and
             other elements that represent the problems and solutions law enforcement confront
             and address within our community. General Order 201.07, Policy Advisory
             Committee, outlines the responsibilities and membership of the committee.
    6. Ride-In Program - The goal of the Ride-In Program is to provide citizens the opportunity
        to observe patrol operations in an informative and safe environment. Guidelines for citizen
        participation and Department approval is located in General Order 207.00, Ride-In
        Procedures.
                                          248
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


    7. Procedural Justice Unit - The mission of the Procedural Justice Unit is to provide training
       and support to the Fort Worth Police Department and citizenry that enhances internal and
       external police legitimacy thereby increasing trust, reducing crime, improving officer and
       public safety and help achieve the goals of our department. Presentations will include, but
       not be limited to,:
        a. Host Citizen Use of Force Scenario training to be conducted quarterly.
        b. Provide training to community groups, leadership, and youth discussing various
            topics such as objectives of the National Initiative, social justice and community
            issues, past and present perceptions related to law enforcement, and how to address
            conflicting issues within our community.
        c. Provide procedural justice training for all sworn officers and to community leaders.
        d. Host meetings for the discussion of implicit bias, procedural justice and reconciliation
            with the City of Fort Worth.
        e. Host meetings for the discussion of intervention for domestic violence and other
            crimes.

347.02 RACIAL PROFILING
The guidelines in this General Order are intended to reaffirm the department's commitment to
unbiased policing in all its encounters between an officer and any person; to reinforce procedures
that serve to ensure public confidence and mutual trust through the provision of services in a fair
and equitable fashion; and to protect officers from unwarranted accusations of misconduct when
acting within the dictates of departmental policy and the law.
A. Officers shall police in a proactive manner and investigate suspected violations of law.
     Officers shall actively enforce state and federal laws in a responsible and professional manner,
     without regard to race, ethnicity or national origin. Officers are strictly prohibited from
     engaging in racial profiling as defined in this order. This order shall be applicable to officer's
     interactions with all persons, whether drivers, passengers or pedestrians.
B. Officers shall conduct themselves in a respectful manner at all times when dealing with the
     public. Two of the fundamental rights guaranteed by both the United States and Texas
     constitutions are equal protection under the law and freedom from unreasonable searches and
     seizures by government agents. The right of all persons to be treated equally and to be free
     from unreasonable searches and seizures must be respected. Racial profiling is an
     unacceptable patrol tactic and is strictly prohibited.
C. This order shall not preclude officers from offering assistance, such as upon observing a
     substance leaking from a vehicle, a flat tire, or someone who appears to be ill, lost or confused.
     Nor does this order prohibit stopping someone suspected of a crime based upon observed
     actions and/or information received about the person.
D. Definitions
     1. Racial Profiling – A law enforcement-initiated action based on an individual’s race,
          ethnicity, or national origin rather than on the individual’s behavior or on information
          identifying the individual as having engaged in criminal activity.
          a. Racial profiling pertains to persons who are viewed as suspects or potential suspects
               of criminal behavior. The term is not relevant as it pertains to witnesses,
               complainants or other citizen contacts.
          b. The prohibition against racial profiling does not preclude the use of race, ethnicity or
               national origin as factors in a detention decision. Race, ethnicity or national origin
               may be legitimate factors in a detention decision when used as part of an actual
                                            249
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


            description of a specific suspect for whom an officer is searching. Detaining an
            individual and conducting an inquiry into that person’s activities simply because of
            that individual’s race, ethnicity or national origin is racial profiling. Examples of
            racial profiling include but are not limited to the following:
            (1) Citing a driver who is speeding in a stream of traffic where most other drivers
                  are speeding because of the cited driver’s race, ethnicity or national origin.
            (2) Stopping or detaining the driver of a vehicle based on the determination that a
                  person of that race, ethnicity or national origin is unlikely to own or possess that
                  specific make or model of vehicle.
            (3) Stopping or detaining an individual based upon the determination that a person
                  of that race, ethnicity or national origin does not belong in a specific part of town
                  or a specific place.
       c. A law enforcement agency can derive these principles from the adoption of this
            definition of racial profiling:
            (1) That law enforcement officers may not use racial or ethnic stereotypes as factors
                  in selecting whom to stop and search.
            (2) Racial profiling is not relevant as it pertains to witnesses, etc.
            (3) That police may not use racial or ethnic stereotypes as factors in selecting whom
                  to stop and search, while police may consider race in conjunction with other
                  known factors of the suspect.
   2. Race or Ethnicity – Of a particular decent, including White, Black, Hispanic or Latino,
       Asian or Pacific Islander, or Alaska Native or American Indian.
   3. Motor Vehicle Stop – A peace officer who stops a motor vehicle for an alleged violation
       of a law or ordinance regulating traffic.
E. Training
   1. Officers are responsible for adhering to all Texas Commission on Law Enforcement
       (TCOLE) training as mandated by law.
   2. All officers shall complete a TCOLE training and education program on racial profiling
       not later than the second anniversary of the date the officer is licensed under Chapter 1701
       of the Texas Occupations Code or the date the officer applies for an intermediate
       proficiency certificate, whichever date is earlier. A person who on September 1, 2001,
       held a TCOLE intermediate proficiency certificate, or who had held a peace officer
       license issued by TCOLE for at least two years, shall complete a TCOLE training and
       education program on racial profiling not later than September 1, 2003.
   3. The Chief of Police, as part of the initial training and continued education for such
       appointment, will be required to attend the LEMIT program on racial profiling.
   4. An individual appointed or elected as a police chief before the effective date of this Act
       shall complete the program on racial profiling established under Subsection (k), Section
       96.641, Education Code.
F. Complaint Investigation
   1. The department shall accept complaints from any person who believes he or she has been
       stopped or searched based on racial, ethnic or national origin profiling. No person shall
       be discouraged, intimidated or coerced from filing a complaint, nor discriminated against
       because he or she filed such a complaint.
   2. If an officer initiating a stop receives an allegation of racial profiling, the officer shall
       provide their name and ID number to the individual with information on how to contact
       Internal Affairs or the officer's supervisor. Any employee contacted shall provide to that
                                            250
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


        person information on the department's process for filing a complaint. All employees will
        report any allegation of racial profiling to their supervisor before the end of their shift.
        a. Officers shall provide information, including telephone number, mailing address, and
             email address for contacting Internal Affairs to any individual who inquires about
             reporting an incident perceived to be racially motivated, or who wishes to generate a
             compliment.
        b. Any supervisor/manager receiving a racial profiling complaint shall notify the
             Internal Affairs Division in a timely manner of the compliant and the action taken.
        c. Supervisors shall monitor the adherence to the General Orders by all employees
             under their command and shall initiate an investigation into all alleged violations
             established under this General Order.
   3. All complaints will be acknowledged in writing to the complainant who will receive
        information regarding the disposition of such complaint within a reasonable period of
        time. The investigation shall be reduced to writing and any reviewer’s comments or
        conclusions shall be sent through the chain of command to the Chief of Police or designee.
        When applicable, findings and/or recommendations for disciplinary action, retraining, or
        changes in policy shall be part of the recommendation to the Chief of Police or designee.
   4. Allegations of misconduct and disciplinary action shall follow the procedures as outlined
        in General Order 410.00. Officers shall be subject to disciplinary action up to and
        including indefinite suspension for engaging in racial profiling.
   5. If there is a departmental video or audio recording of the events upon which a complaint
        of racial profiling is based, upon commencement of an investigation into the complaint
        and written request of the officer made the subject of the complaint, this department shall
        promptly provide a copy of the recording to that officer.
G. Public Education
   The police department will inform the public of its guidelines against racial profiling and the
   compliment and complaint process. Methods that may be utilized to inform the public of the
   process are news media, radio, service or civic presentations, the Internet, as well as governing
   board meetings. With respect to each ticket, citation, or warning issued by an officer, the
   telephone number, mailing address, and email address for Internal Affairs shall be provided
   either on the warning, ticket, or citation or by other methods directed by the department (i.e.
   business cards, flyers, stickers, etc). Additionally, information will be made available as
   appropriate in languages other than English.
H. Data Collection and Reporting
   1. Data shall be collected on all motor vehicle stops. Information will be collected on the
        driver only. The officer shall promptly enter all data required by law into the Motor
        Vehicle Stop Checklist database before the end of the duty shift. The form may be found
        on the Fort Worth Police internal portal under Racial Profiling.
   2. Any vehicle equipped with video and/or audio capabilities shall retain the video and/or
        audio documentation in accordance with the division’s standard operating procedures.
        Such documentation shall be retained for at least 180 days after the stop, or until
        disposition if a complaint has been made.
        a. If a complaint has been made, the documentation shall be retained by the Internal
             Affairs Division until final disposition of the complaint, if not longer as required
             under other laws or policies.
   3. Internal Affairs shall be responsible for compiling the number of racial profiling
        complaints and forwarding this information to Policy Management at the end of the year.
                                           251
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


     4.  At the direction of the Chief of Police or designee, additional data may be collected by
         the department in an effort to monitor enforcement actions and to provide a overview of
         department compliance with this General Order.
     5. An annual report will be prepared or coordinated by Policy Management based on the
         data collection and in accordance with TCOLE guidelines and forwarded to the city
         manager within the prescribed time period for distribution to the City Council.
I.   Use of Video and Audio Equipment
     1. Each traffic stop made by an officer that is capable of being recorded by video and/or
         audio shall be recorded.
     2. Data recorded will follow requirements of General Order 506.03, Officer-Worn Digital
         Recording Devices, and General Order 506.04, In-Car Recording System.

347.03 BIAS-FREE POLICING
A. Purpose and Scope
    1. It is the policy of the Fort Worth Police Department to treat all persons with dignity,
       respect and professionalism. The Fort Worth Police Department provides police
       services to the community in a nonpartisan, fair, equitable, and objective manner
       without consideration of race, color, gender, age, national origin, religion, disability,
       economic status, sexual orientation, gender expression, gender identity, transgender
       status, membership in a cultural group, or other individual characteristics or
       distinctions.
    2. Equal treatment provides that persons, irrespective of race or other distinction shall be
       treated in the same basic manner under the same or similar circumstances. Equal
       treatment does not mean all persons in the same or similar circumstances can or must be
       treated identically in all cases. Reasonable considerations and/or accommodations may
       be made when dealing with individuals with physical or mental disabilities, infirmity,
       illnesses or similar conditions or when information about them necessitates different
       treatment.
B. Definitions
    1. Biased Policing - Discrimination in the performance of duties, based on personal
       prejudices or partiality of officers, that interferes with their professional judgment,
       training or adherence to law. Biased policing includes, but is not limited to, making
       prejudicial decisions affecting individuals in classes protected by federal, state and local
       law.
    2. Gender expression - Person’s external characteristics and behaviors including, but not
       limited to, dress, grooming, mannerisms, speech patterns and social interactions that are
       socially identified with a particular gender.
    3. Gender identity - Person’s innate, deeply felt sense of gender, which may or may not
       correspond to the person’s physical body or sex listed on their original birth certificate.
    4. Sexual orientation - Heterosexuality, homosexuality or bisexuality or being identified
       with such orientation.
    5. Transgender - Person who experiences and/or expresses their gender differently from
       conventional or cultural expectations including, but not limited to, those who express a
       gender that does not match the sex listed on their original birth certificate or who
       physically alter their sex.



                                           252
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


         a.  Intersex individuals - Individuals who, because of their chromosomal make-up or
             other biological reasons are born with physical characteristics that make their
             biological sex ambiguous.
        b. Cross-dressers - Individuals whose gender identity matches their birth-assigned
             sex, but who sometimes prefer to wear clothes not traditionally associated with
             their sex. Most individuals who consider themselves cross-dressers do not wear
             cross-gendered attire all of the time. The term "cross-dressers" should not be used
             to refer to individuals who are living as members of the opposite sex, in accordance
             with their gender identity.
        c. Transsexual - An older term, that originated in the medical and psychological
             communities, and which is used to refer to individuals who wish to change, or have
             changed their birth-assigned sex, through hormones, surgery or other physical
             procedures. Just as many gay people prefer the term "gay" to the term
             "homosexual," many transgender people prefer "transgender" to “transsexual."
             Some transgender people, however, still prefer to use the medical term to describe
             themselves.
C. Limitations
   1. Bias-based policing is prohibited both in enforcement of the law and delivery of police
        services.
   2. Officers shall not use race, color, gender, age, national origin, religion, disability,
        economic status, sexual orientation, gender expression, gender identity, transgender
        status, membership in a cultural group, or an individual's ability/inability to speak English
        as the criteria for determining when or how to take enforcement action or pro- vide police
        services.
   3. Nothing in this order prohibits officers from using the traits and characteristics of persons,
        such as race, ethnicity, or national origin, in combination with other facts, to assist in
        establishing reasonable suspicion or probable cause in the same manner that officers
        would use descriptions such as a specific hair color, height, gender or other identifying
        traits.
   4. Officers shall not unreasonably endanger themselves or another person to conform to this
        General Order.
D. Any employee(s) who witness or are aware of instances of bias-based policing shall report the
   incident to their supervisor immediately.
E. Gender Classification Guidelines for Transgender Individuals
   1. Officers shall:
        a. Consider a person transgender if the person identifies themselves as transgender or,
             if upon reasonable belief that person may be transgender, the officer asks and
             receives an affirmative response.
        b. Respectfully treat individuals in a manner appropriate to the individual’s gender, or
             gender identity/expression when known,
        c. Use pronouns as requested by the individual ( e.g., “she, her, hers” for an individual
             who self-identifies as a female; “he, him, his” for an individual who self-identifies
             as a male). If officers are uncertain by which gender the individual wishes to be
             addressed, they will respectfully ask the individual for clarification,
        d. When requested, address the individual by the name based on their gender identity
             rather than that which is on their government issued identification, and

                                            253
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


         e.  Avoid unnecessary personal questions regarding an individual’s anatomy, transition
             status or sexual history.
    2.   Officers shall not:
         a. Stop, detain, frisk, or search any person for the sole purpose of determining that
             person’s gender or in order to call attention to that person’s gender
             identity/expression, unless following the established department procedures
             regarding the proper processing of arrestees,
         b. Except when legally necessary, such as processing an arrest, either require proof of
             an individual’s gender or challenge an individual’s gender identity/expression,
         c. Use language that a reasonable person would consider demeaning or derogatory; in
             particular, language aimed at a person’s actual or perceived gender, gender
             identity/expression, or sexual orientation,
         d. Disclose an individual’s gender identity or sexual orientation to other arrestees,
             members of the public, or other governmental personnel, absent a proper law
             enforcement purpose,
         e. Make assumptions about an individual’s sexual orientation based upon an
             individual’s gender or gender identity/expression, or
         f. Use a person’s gender or gender identity/expression alone as reasonable suspicion
             that the individual is or has engaged in a crime.

347.04 NUISANCE ABATEMENT
A. The Texas Nuisance Abatement Statutes, found in Chapter 125 of the Texas Civil Practice &
    Remedies Code and Section 101.70 of the Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code (TABC), permit
    law enforcement agencies to close any piece of property involved in illegal activities, such as
    violations of the Texas Penal Code, the Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code (TABC), and the
    Texas Controlled Substances Act. Nuisance abatement is a civil action initiated by the Office
    of the Attorney General and the Fort Worth Police Department against a real property location,
    and the owner of the real property. Action which may be taken against the property owner
    depending on the nature of the nuisance abatement are:
    1. Property closure for a period of six (6) months to one (1) year, once the property has been
         determined to be a nuisance and after a successful suit, unless a surety bond is posted by
         the property owner.
    2. If a surety bond is posted and the illegal activity continues in violation of the court order
         and in violation of the bond, the bond may be forfeited and the property may be
         mandatorily closed for a period of one (1) year.
B. Officers determining that a particular property may constitute a common nuisance based on
    statutes will include any of the following documentation to assist in developing a case:
    1. A written, sworn deposition from the officer denoting the types of activity observed,
         whether the officer has reason to believe the illegal activity will continue if abatement
         action is not taken, and the specific basis for this belief.
    2. Offense/incident reports pertaining to the property in question.
    3. General complaint citations pertaining to the property in question.
C. It shall be the responsibility of the investigating officer(s) to compile the information and
    statistical data on the particular property and present the file through their chain for submission
    to the Attorney General's office. The assigned officer shall be responsible for updating
    information to the Attorney General’s office through reports from the involved division.

Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


347.05 CRIME STOPPERS
A. Philosophy
At its core, community-oriented policing stresses the importance of police and citizens working as
co-producers of police services. The community-oriented policing philosophy sees the two groups
as jointly responsible for reducing crime and improving the quality of life in local neighborhoods.
Law enforcement agencies often rely on assistance from their local citizens and communities for
tips and other information to progress through investigations. Without police/community
engagement, a vast majority of crimes would remain unresolved.
B. Purpose
The purpose of citizen-involved criminal investigation programs is to work with the Fort Worth
community to increase the likelihood of solving crimes which may have few investigative leads
and might otherwise remain unsolved.
C. Crime Stoppers
It is the policy of the Fort Worth Police Department to actively engage with our community citizens
and stake holders during the criminal investigation process through anonymous tip lines, public
outreach, as well as any other citizen-driven information formats in order to identify persons and
property related to offenses and build strong criminal cases for prosecution.
       1. Crime Stoppers of Tarrant County and the Crime Stoppers Detail are governed by Texas
           Government Code Chapter 414, Texas Crime Stoppers Council.
       2. The Crime Stoppers Detail is responsible for the local administration of the Tarrant
           County Crime Stoppers program.
       3. The Crime Stoppers Detail shall research each tip received from Tarrant County Crime
           Stoppers for actionable intelligence before assigning it to the appropriate Unit, Detective,
           or Officer.
           a. If a tip requires reassignment, the assigned unit/officer shall notify the Crime
                Stoppers Detail who will assess reassigning the tip. If there is a disagreement as to
                tip assignment, the INTEX supervisor will determine what unit the tip is to be
                assigned.
           b. The employee assigned a tip shall update the Crime Stoppers Detail every thirty (30)
                days on the status of the tip until it is resolved.
           c. Due to the lengthy nature of their investigations, Narcotics and Vice shall, within
                ninety (90) days, notify the Crime Stoppers Detail of the receipt of the tip and to
                whom the case will be assigned. Updates are required every ninety (90) days until
                the tip is resolved.
       4. Once the tip is resolved, the employee assigned the tip shall notify the Crime Stoppers
           Detail of the resolution (ex: cleared by arrest; unfounded; already known, unable to
           locate, etc.) via the disposition form located in the original tip email. The email can be
           resent at any time by contacting the Crime Stoppers Detail.
       5. Tip information is privileged information, per Government Code 414; therefore, tip
           information shall NOT be placed into a case file. The existence of a tip may be referenced,
           but obtaining a copy of a tip is at the discretion of a judge via subpoena.
       6. If the tip is cleared by arrest, the employee assigned the tip shall provide the Crime
           Stoppers Detail with the details via the disposition form provided in the original tip email,
           including but not limited to:
           a. arrested persons
           b. seized property
           c. case number
                                             255
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


    7. The Crime Stoppers Detail shall report the disposition of the tip to the Tarrant County
       Crime Stoppers.
D. Campus Crime Stoppers
   1. Campus Crime Stoppers of Tarrant County is governed by Texas Government Code
       Chapter 414, Texas Crime Stoppers Council.
   2. Campus Crime Stoppers provides a platform for students in multiple school districts
       within the City of Fort Worth to report campus crimes and to come forward when they
       have information regarding criminal activity or quality of life issues (school policy
       violations, bullying, suicidal, etc.) and remain anonymous.
   3. When a Campus Crime Stoppers tip is received, the Campus Crime Stoppers Detail shall
       ensure the tip is forwarded to the appropriate SRO, the SRO supervisor, and/or school
       staff as appropriate. If there is a disagreement as to tip assignment, the INTEX supervisor
       will determine what unit the tip is to be assigned.
       a. If the tip is received during school hours, the Campus Crime Stoppers Detail may
            follow up by contacting the SRO directly to confirm the tip was received. If after
            hours and a tip contains critical safety information, the Campus Crime Stoppers
            Detail will notify the assigned SRO via phone call.
       b. The assigned SRO shall follow the guidelines in Section C when investigating the
            tip. The SRO should attempt to obtain a disposition on the assigned tip within two
            (2) business days and submit that disposition via the disposition form in the original
            email within thirty (30) days.
       c. The Campus Crime Stoppers Detail shall follow up with the SRO every thirty (30)
            days to obtain disposition of the tip until it is closed.
       d. The Campus Crime Stoppers Detail shall report the disposition of the tip to Tarrant
            County Crime Stoppers.
E. Top Ten Most Wanted Bulletin
   1. The Top Ten Most Wanted Bulletin is a weekly posting of the City of Fort Worth’s top
       ten most wanted criminals produced by the Crime Stoppers Detail. In the absence of
       requested suspects, the Crime Stoppers Detail shall select new subjects for the bulletin
       from active FWPD felony warrants that have been active for over three (3) months.
   2. Detectives or other personnel interested in placing suspects on the Top Ten Most Wanted
       Bulletin should contact the Crime Stoppers Detail for guidance. When requesting placing
       suspects on the Top Ten Most Wanted Bulletin, detectives or other personnel should
       provide the Crime Stoppers Detail with quality still photographs of the suspect, if
       available.

                         349.00       GUN SHOT DETECTION
349.01 GUN SHOT DETECTION TBP 7.36
It is the policy of the Fort Worth Police Department to use Gun Shot Detection (GSD) for official
law enforcement purposes that will promote the health, safety, and welfare of residents, officers,
and visitors, consistent with legal and constitutional limitations, privacy concerns, and accepted
ethical standards. The purpose of this order is to establish procedures for the response and

                                           256
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


investigation into violent crimes and incidents involving gunfire, while safeguarding all civil
liberties.
A. Definitions
     1. Gun Shot Detection (GSD) system - Technology that detects outdoor audible gunfire
           within the coverage area using acoustic sensors capable of pinpointing the accurate
           location of a gunfire event.
     2. Coverage Area - A defined perimeter where the gun shot detection system sensors can
           reliably triangulate incidents of gunfire.
B. The Real Time Crime Center (RTCC) will monitor all gun shot detection alerts and attempt
     to verify the legitimacy of each alert. RTCC will initiate a “shots fired in area” (SIG 77) for
     any alerts that can be verified through audio, video, or other sources.
     1. If RTCC personnel feel that the call requires a more immediate response, the officer can
           elevate the call to priority 1 with additional information to be provided to responding
           officers.
C. RTCC personnel shall provide the responding officers with a location of the suspected gunfire.
D. Responding officers should take a safe and strategic approach to the incident, being aware that
     an offender or multiple offenders may be on scene.
E. Responding officers should consider requesting necessary resources to the scene, such as
     Directed Response, Air Support, and/or drone assets.
F. Responding officers shall follow any relevant procedures in the investigation to include
     General Order 329.00, Person with a Gun, and General Order 302.00, Active Shooter
     Response, as appropriate.
G. An arrest must be based on the totality of circumstances gathered from a thorough
     investigation and reaching the threshold of probable cause; therefore, officers shall not arrest
     solely on a gun shot detection alert. The gun shot detection alert is a lead only; any possible
     connection or involvement of any subject to the gun shot detection alert must be determined
     through further investigation and investigative resources.
H. Responding officers should canvas within one hundred (100) feet of the gun shot detection
     location for victims, witnesses, and evidence. Any casings, firearms, and magazines recovered
     on the scene shall be considered evidentiary.
I. Responding officers shall notify the RTCC should it become clear that the gun shot detection
     alert was false.
J. If an Incident Report is generated, the officer shall designate within the report narrative that
     the incident is Gun Shot Detection-related.

           350.00        AUTOMATED LICENSE PLATE DETECTION
350.01 PURPOSE AND SCOPE (Revised 9/11/2026) TBP 7.36
A. This General Order establishes the authorized uses, prohibited uses, access controls, query
    documentation standards, retention limits, sharing restrictions, auditing requirements, and
    disciplinary consequences governing the Fort Worth Police Department's (FWPD) use of
    Automated License Plate Recognition (ALPR) technology, including the Flock Safety
    platform and any successor or comparable system.
B. This order applies to every person who accesses, queries, receives, stores, transmits, or
    otherwise uses FWPD ALPR data, without exception. This includes sworn officers, civilian
    employees, and personnel of other agencies or departments operating under data-sharing
    agreement(s) with the Fort Worth Police Department.
                                            257
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


C. This order also governs FWPD access to ALPR data owned by other agencies or by private
   parties, including data made available through network sharing.
D. This order sets internal Fort Worth Police Department standards, the violation of which is
   grounds for discipline up to and including termination and, where warranted, criminal
   prosecution.

350.02 POLICY STATEMENT
A. It is the policy of the Fort Worth Police Department that ALPR technology is a legitimate and
    effective investigative tool that will be used exclusively for Authorized Law Enforcement
    Purposes, subject to continuous auditing, and administered in a manner that preserves public
    trust.
B. Accordingly, the Fort Worth Police Department will operate its ALPR program on the
    presumption of transparency and verification: every query is logged, every query is
    attributable to an authorized user, and every query is subject to review.
C. Employees have no expectation of privacy in their use of the ALPR system. All activity is
    recorded and monitored.

350.03 DEFINITIONS
A. ALPR System - Any technology that captures images of vehicles and license plates, converts
    license plate characters to machine-readable text, associates the read with a date, time, and
    location, and stores or transmits that information. This includes fixed, mobile, and any
    associated analytic tools, including vehicle-fingerprint search, convoy analysis, or similar
    functions.
B. ALPR Data - Any license plate read, associated image, vehicle-descriptor data (make, model,
    color, distinguishing features), geolocation, timestamp, alert record, query record, audit log,
    derivative product, or other data generated by an ALPR System.
C. Query - Any search, lookup, retrieval, filter, or analytic operation run within a ALPR System,
    whether by license plate, partial license plate, vehicle description, geographic area, time
    window, or any other parameter.
D. Hot List - A list of license plates for which the ALPR system generates an automated alert
    upon a matching read.
E. Alert (or Hit) - An automated system notification that a captured license plate matched a Hot
    List entry. An Alert is an investigative lead only.
F. Authorized User - An individual who has completed required training, has been assigned a
    unique named account by the ALPR Program Manager, and whose access has not been
    suspended or revoked.
G. Case Code -The FWPD Records Management System (RMS) case number, incident number,
    or other Fort Worth Police Department-approved control number entered by the user at the
    time of a Query to identify the specific investigation the Query supports.
H. Network Sharing - Any configuration by which FWPD ALPR Data is made accessible to an
    external agency, or by which FWPD users access ALPR Data owned by an external agency,
    including regional, statewide, and national sharing arrangements offered by the vendor.
I. Authorized Law Enforcement Purpose - A specific, articulable, and documented purpose
    connected to:
    1. A criminal investigation,
    2. An active criminal or civil-commitment warrant,
    3. A missing or endangered person,
                                           258
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


    4.  A stolen vehicle or stolen license plate,
    5.  Active statewide alert,
    6.  An immediate threat to life or public safety, or
    7.  An authorized administrative search, audit, training, or system-testing function by the
        ALPR Program Manager or ALPR Audit Authority.
J. ALPR Program Manager – Designated administrator(s) of the ALPR System and designees
   assigned to the Real-Time Crime Center (RTCC).
K. ALPR Audit Authority – Designated by the Chief of Police independent of the ALPR Program
   Manager, currently the Professional Standards Division.

350.04 LEGAL FRAMEWORK
A. The restrictions in this order are adopted as a matter of Fort Worth Police Department policy
    and City governance, not as a recitation of state statutory mandates. Should the Legislature
    enact ALPR-specific requirements, this order shall be amended within ninety (90) days of the
    effective date of that legislation.

350.05 AUTHORIZED USES
A. ALPR Data may be accessed or queried only for an Authorized Law Enforcement Purpose as
    defined in General Order 350.03 I, and only where the user can articulate a factual connection
    between the Query and that purpose at the time the Query is run.
B. The user must have, at minimum, reasonable suspicion that the vehicle, license plate, or
    location queried is connected to criminal activity, or one of the exigent or status-based grounds
    enumerated in General Order 350.03 I.
C. Every Query shall be supported by a valid Case Code entered at the time of the Query, except
    as provided in General Order 350.08 E.
D. Historical Query scope shall be no broader than necessary. A Query returning more than thirty
    (30) days of historical data, or outside of Texas, requires approval of the ALPR Program
    Manager, to be documented in the Query record.

350.06 PROHIBITED USES
A. Each of the following prohibited uses is a separate violation, regardless of the harm or further
    use of the information:
    1. Querying the ALPR system for any personal, private, curiosity-driven, financial,
        romantic, familial, or social reason.
    2. Knowingly querying a license plate or vehicle associated with a current or former spouse,
        intimate partner, romantic interest, family member, neighbor, acquaintance, co-worker,
        or any person with whom the user has or has had a personal relationship, absent an
        assigned investigation, prior written approval from a Lieutenant or above, and full
        disclosure of the relationship where exigent factors, as outlined in General Order 350.08E
        are present and would prevent reassigning the query to an independent user.
    3. Without authorization, querying, or causing another to query, on behalf of any person
        who is not an Authorized User, including other employees whose access has been
        suspended or revoked.
    4. Querying based on race, ethnicity, color, national origin, religion, sex, gender identity,
        sexual orientation, disability, housing status, or perceived immigration status, or on any
        factor other than articulable facts connecting the vehicle or location to an Authorized Law
        Enforcement Purpose.
                                            259
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


    5. Self-queries are prohibited. A user shall not query the user's own vehicle, license plate,
       or residence except as part of a documented system test performed by the ALPR Program
       Manager or the ALPR Audit Authority.
   6. Absent a documented criminal predicate;
       a. Querying to identify vehicles at:
            (1) Reproductive health providers
            (2) Mental health or substance use treatment facilities
            (3) Immigration legal service providers
            (4) Domestic violence shelters
            (5) Places of Worship, or
       b. Querying for the purpose of identifying, monitoring, or cataloging persons engaged
            in activity protected by the First Amendment, including:
            (1) Attendance at protests
            (2) Demonstrations
            (3) Political events
            (4) Places of Worship
            (5) Union activity, or meetings of advocacy organizations.
   7. Entering a false, generic, misleading, or non-responsive Case Code or reason for a Query,
       including entries such as "investigation," "patrol," "test," "training," "traffic," or a case
       number unrelated to the Query.
   8. Using ALPR Data for any non-City related, administrative, employment, licensing, code
       enforcement, debt collection, insurance, custody, divorce, or immigration-status-only
       matter that is not part of a criminal investigation, except where disclosure is compelled
       by court order, subpoena, or law.
   9. Selling, trading, leasing, bartering, or receiving anything of value in exchange for ALPR
       Data or access to it.
   10. Sharing account credentials, allowing another person to use an account, or accessing the
       system using another person's credentials, under any circumstance.
   11. Disabling, circumventing, obstructing, or attempting to defeat any audit, logging, case-
       code, multi-factor authentication, or access-control feature of the ALPR system.
   12. Retaliating in any manner against any employee or member of the public who reports,
       questions, or cooperates in the investigation of suspected ALPR misuse.
   13. Initiating a vehicle stop, detention, arrest, or use of force based solely on an unverified
       ALPR Alert as noted in General Order 350.10.
B. Ignorance of the requirements of this order is not a defense.

350.07 SYSTEM ACCESS AND USER ACCOUNTABILITY
A. Access is a privilege granted by the ALPR Program Manager, not an entitlement of rank or
    assignment. Access shall be granted only to personnel with a demonstrated, ongoing need
    arising from their assignment. Completion of the initial certification training established by
    the Fort Worth Police Department is a condition of access and annual recertification training
    will be required.
B. Every Authorized User shall be issued a unique, individually named account. Shared, generic,
    unit-level, or "role" accounts are prohibited. Every Query must be attributable to an
    Authorized User.
C. Multi-factor authentication shall be enabled and enforced for all accounts at all times. It shall
    not be disabled for any user for any reason.
                                           260
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


D. Access shall be granted only after the user has:
   1. Completed initial certification training,
   2. Signed the ALPR User Acknowledgment acknowledging the terms of this order, and
   3. Been assigned a permission level no greater than required by the user's duties.
E. Permission levels shall be tiered. Administrative privileges — including the ability to modify
   Hot Lists, alter sharing settings, add or remove users, or change retention configuration —
   shall be limited to the ALPR Program Manager and designees assigned to the Real-Time
   Crime Center. The Assistant Chief of Special Operations and Investigative Bureau or their
   designee will provide a list of Authorized Users with administrative privileges in writing to
   the Chief of Police annually.
F. Access shall be terminated within twenty-four (24) hours of a user's separation from the Fort
   Worth Police Department, transfer to an assignment without an ongoing need, placement on
   administrative leave, or suspension of law enforcement authority. The ALPR Program
   Manager shall reconcile the active user roster against the Human Resources active-employee
   roster monthly and shall document each reconciliation.

350.08 QUERY STANDARDS AND DOCUMENTATION
A. Every Query shall record, at minimum:
    1. User's identity,
    2. Date and time,
    3. Search parameters,
    4. Case Code,
    5. Networks searched, and
    6. Results returned.
B. Case Codes shall be mandatory for all Queries. The Fort Worth Police Department shall enable
    and maintain the vendor's mandatory case-code configuration and shall not disable it.
C. ALPR Queries are directed at vehicles, license plates, and locations, as defined in General
    Order 350.05.
D. Exigent Bypass. Where an immediate threat to life or public safety prevents contemporaneous
    entry of a Case Code, the user may invoke the exigency bypass. Every bypassed Query is
    automatically flagged, is subject to one-hundred-percent review, and shall be justified in
    writing by the user, and reviewed by RTCC staff, before the end of the user's next shift.
E. Queries returning results used in any investigative report, affidavit, warrant application, or
    court proceeding shall be documented in the case file, including the date of the Query, the
    parameters used, and the Case Code.

350.09 HOT LIST MANAGEMENT
A. A license plate may be added to a Fort Worth Police Department-managed Hot List only where
    there is reasonable suspicion that the associated vehicle is connected to criminal activity, an
    active warrant, a stolen vehicle or license plate report, a missing or endangered person, or an
    active statewide alert. Hot lists will be approved and managed by the Real Time Crime Center.
    All Hot List entry requests must be submitted through the Fort Worth Police Departmental
    portal for approval.
B. Each Hot List entry shall record the entering user, the date, the Case Code, the offense, and a
    mandatory expiration date not to exceed thirty (30) days. Entries may be renewed only upon
    documented supervisory review confirming the underlying basis still exists and routed to the
    Real Time Crime Center for final approval.
                                           261
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


C. Hot List entries shall be removed within twenty-four (24) hours of the Fort Worth Police
   Department learning that the underlying warrant, report, or investigative basis is no longer
   valid. Upon taking action on a Hot List alert, the Authorized User shall contact RTCC to clear
   the Hot List alert.
D. The ALPR Program Manager or designee shall audit all active Hot List entries monthly for
   validity, expiration, and documentation, and shall report results to the ALPR Audit Authority.

350.10 ALERT VERIFICATION AND FIELD RESPONSE
A. An officer may not detain an individual based on an alert from the ALPR system unless the
    officer has reasonable suspicion that such person is involved in criminal activity. Each
    incident should be weighed according to the totality of circumstances.
B. Before initiating any enforcement action based on an Alert, the officer shall:
    1. Visually compare the license plate on the vehicle to the license plate in the Alert, character
         by character, including the state of issuance and any stacked, obscured, or specialty
         characters; or
    2. Confirm through dispatch, TCIC/NCIC, RTCC or the originating agency that the
         underlying warrant, stolen report, or Hot List basis is current and valid; or
    3. If the ALPR Alert cannot be confirmed through dispatch, TCIC/NCIC, RTCC or the
         originating agency, officers should independently establish reasonable suspicion or
         probable cause for the stop.
C. Where the vehicle make, model, color, or other descriptor does not match the Alert record,
    the officer shall not initiate a stop solely on the Alert alone.
D. The officer shall document in the offense or incident report that verification under General
    Order 350.10 B above was completed, including the method and the dispatch or TCIC/NCIC
    confirmation.
E. Any stop initiated on an Alert later determined to be erroneous shall be reported to the ALPR
    Program Manager within twenty-four (24) hours. The ALPR Audit Authority shall track
    erroneous-stop incidents, analyze root cause, and report quarterly under General Order
    350.13E.

350.11 DATA RETENTION AND DESTRUCTION
A. General retention. ALPR Data that does not result in an Alert and is not associated with a
    documented investigation shall be automatically and permanently deleted at the expiration of
    the retention period. The Fort Worth Police Department shall configure a retention period no
    longer than thirty (30) days
B. Evidentiary retention. ALPR Data relevant to an open investigation, a pending prosecution, a
    claim, or a litigation hold shall be exported to the case file or moved to the vendor's evidentiary
    storage mode before expiration. Retention thereafter is governed by the City of Fort Worth
    retention policy, applicable Texas State Library and Archives Commission records retention
    schedule and Tex. Loc. Gov't Code ch. 202 and 203, not by this section.
C. Query logs, audit logs, access logs, and disclosure records shall be preserved for a minimum
    of 2.5 years (30 Months), and the vendor contract shall require the vendor to preserve and
    produce them for that period. Log retention shall exceed image retention so that misuse
    remains detectable after the underlying images are gone.
D. No Authorized User shall have the ability to alter or delete audit logs, query records, or
    disclosure records. The ALPR Program Manager shall confirm this configuration in writing
    to the ALPR Audit Authority quarterly.
                                            262
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders



350.12 DATA SHARING, EXTERNAL ACCESS, AND NETWORK PARTICIPATION
A. ALPR data may be protected from public disclosure under section 552.108(b) of the Texas
    Government Code. All requests to withhold this data must be submitted to the Attorney
    General for review and ruling.
B. Compelled disclosure. Nothing in this Section prohibits disclosure required by court order,
    subpoena, discovery obligation, the Texas Public Information Act, or state law. All such
    disclosures shall be reviewed by the City Attorney's Office and recorded in the Disclosure
    Register.

350.13 AUDITING AND REAL-TIME MISUSE DETECTION
    This Section is the operative accountability mechanism of this order. Audit obligations are
    mandatory, not discretionary, and are not contingent on a complaint, allegation, or media
    inquiry.
A. Audit Authority and Independence
    1. Auditing of the ALPR system is conducted in real time via an Audit Alert tool. Any Audit
        alerts will be the responsibility of the Professional Standards Division and the chain of
        command of the user. The Professional Standards Division will receive audit alerts and
        make an initial assessment of any potential policy violations and alert the user’s chain of
        command. Any search in violation of this policy will be logged into the BlueTeam system
        and routed to the chain of command for review.
    2. The ALPR Audit Authority, currently the Professional Standards Division, shall have
        unrestricted read access to all query logs, audit logs, user rosters, Hot Lists, sharing
        configurations, and Disclosure Register entries, and shall not require the permission of
        the ALPR Program Manager to obtain them.
    3. No person shall audit that person's own Queries. Where an audit implicates the ALPR
        Program Manager or a member of the ALPR Audit Authority, the matter shall be referred
        immediately to the Special Operations and Investigations Bureau Assistant Chief and to
        the Chief of Police.
B. Real-Time and Continuous Automated Auditing
    1. The Fort Worth Police Department shall enable and continuously utilize the vendor's
        automated audit and anomaly-detection capability (currently marketed as "Audit
        Assist"), which applies real-time analysis to identify search patterns inconsistent with
        normal agency use. This capability shall be enabled at all times and shall not be
        disabled, degraded, or reconfigured to reduce sensitivity without the written
        approval of the Chief of Police, with notice to the Assistant City Manager.
    2. The Fort Worth Police Department will enable the vendor's proactive lockout capability,
        which automatically suspends a user's access when activity meets abnormal-behavior
        criteria, pending administrative review.
    3. Automated alerts shall be checked twice a week by Professional Standards Division.
C. Random Sampling Audits
    1. Monthly random sample. The Professional Standards Division shall audit, each month, a
        random sample of 100 Queries.
    2. Selection integrity. Sample selection shall be generated by a random-number method that
        is not controlled, previewed, or influenced by the ALPR Program Manager.
    3. Review standard. For each sampled Query the auditor shall verify:
        (a) A valid Case Code was entered;
                                           263
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


       (b) The case exists in the RMS, is genuine, and was open and assigned at the time of the
            Query;
       (c) The queried license plate, vehicle, or location bears an articulable connection to that
            case;
       (d) The reason field states facts sufficient to establish an Authorized Law Enforcement
            Purpose;
       (e) The scope of the Query — time span, geographic breadth, networks searched — was
            proportionate; and
       (f) Any required ALPR Program Manager authorization required was obtained and
            documented.
D. Systematic One-Hundred-Percent Audits
   1. Independent of the random sample, the Professional Standards Division shall review one
       hundred percent (100%) of the following categories every month:
       (a) All Queries invoking the exigency bypass under General Order 350.08;
       (b) All Queries with a blank, generic, or non-responsive reason field;
E. Quarterly and Annual Audits
   1. Quarterly comprehensive audit. The ALPR Audit Authority shall conduct a quarterly
       audit addressing, at minimum: amount of total scans, amount of Queries and Alerts, and
       verified Alerts; per-user Query counts with statistical outlier detection;        case-code
       compliance rate; flag generation, triage timeliness, and disposition; erroneous-stop
       incidents; Hot List validity; user-roster reconciliation; sharing-configuration
       reconciliation; and Disclosure Register review. Results shall be reported in writing to
       the Chief of Police.
   2. Referral. Where an audit identifies conduct that may violate General Order 350.06 of this
       order, the ALPR Audit Authority shall:
       (a) Suspend the user's access immediately,
       (b) Preserve all associated logs,
       (c) Refer the matter to Professional Standards Division within one (1) business day, and
       (d) Where the conduct may constitute a criminal offense, refer the matter to the Special
            Investigations Unit for further investigation. Referral is mandatory and is not subject
            to the discretion of the ALPR Program Manager or the user's chain of command.
   3. Annual independent audit. The Fort Worth Police Department shall commission an
       annual audit of the ALPR program by the City’s Internal Auditor or a qualified
       independent party with no pre-existing financial relationship to the ALPR vendor or the
       city. The independent audit shall assess policy compliance, query justification
       quality, audit-program effectiveness, sharing configurations, retention compliance,
       discipline consistency, training compliance, and program efficacy. The report shall be
       delivered to the Chief of Police, the City Manager, and the City Council.
   4. Audit records. All audit work product, samples, findings, and dispositions shall be
       retained for a minimum of 2.5 years by the City Secretary’s Office, and shall be produced
       to the City Attorney's Office, the City Manager’s Office, or an independent auditor on
       request.

350.14 TRAINING
A. No person shall be granted ALPR access before completing Fort Worth Police Department-
    approved initial training covering: the technology and its limitations, legal framework;
    authorized and prohibited uses; case code and reason-field standards; alert verification
                                           264
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


   requirements; sharing restrictions; the audit program; the duty to report; and disciplinary
   consequences for misuse.
B. All Authorized Users shall complete annual refresher training. Access shall be suspended
   automatically for any user whose refresher training is more than thirty (30) days overdue.
   ALPR access accounts that have not been used for six (6) months will automatically be
   deactivated and completion of the annual certification course will be required to reactivate the
   ALPR access account.
C. Training records shall be maintained in accordance with TCOLE requirements.


                    351.00        SPECIALIZED PATROL UNITS

351.01 BICYCLE PATROL UNIT
A. The primary functions of Bicycle Patrol are to deter street crime and increase the public
    perception of safety for citizens in certain target areas through response to violations of the
    penal statutes, public relations, and crime prevention education.
B. Bicycle Patrol Unit(s) shall develop and maintain a SOP relating to operation of the Bicycle
    Patrol and the response to citizen and community needs within their geographic assigned area.
C. A Fort Worth Police Department approved certification and all subsequent training shall be
    coordinated through the administrative supervisor of the Central Bicycle Patrol Unit and the
    assigned training coordinator of Bicycle Patrol. The Central Division Bicycle Patrol Unit shall
    maintain a sufficient number of certified instructors to allow for periodic certification and
    refresher classes for qualified officers.
D. For the safety of the officers, all officers assigned part-time or full-time to patrol on a bicycle
    shall be certified prior to assignment to bicycle patrol. If an officer is not certified and is
    assigned to bicycle patrol, the officer must ride with a certified officer until attaining the
    certification.
E. Officers assigned to bicycle patrol duties in any division shall wear the prescribed uniform
    and maintain the bicycle specifications as stated in the General Orders and the Central
    Division's Bike Patrol Unit Standard Operating Procedures.

351.02 MOUNTED PATROL UNIT
A. The Mounted Patrol Unit is responsible for improving the department’s image through the
    application of crime prevention measures and by establishing credibility and support for the
    department through positive contact with citizens of the community and visitors to the city.
    The Mounted Patrol Unit is also responsible for deterring street crime and increasing the
    public perception of safety for citizens.
B. Mounted Patrol officers shall handle all on-view offenses, arrests, and minor accidents unless
    circumstances make it impossible for them to do so.
C. Due to the Mounted Patrol Unit’s limited mobility, the patrol officer shall maintain original
    priority on calls for service within the area patrolled. Any call requiring the officer to change
    location to complete the investigation shall be dispatched to the appropriate division officer,
    whenever possible.
D. The Mounted Patrol Unit shall maintain a high level of training in crowd control and crowd
    movement techniques.

              354.00        EMERGENCY CONTROL PROCEDURES
354.01 PURPOSE
To establish guidelines for police response to emergency situations involving disasters and civil
disorders. These procedures were developed to coordinate the use of equipment and personnel
resources to maintain or restore order, provide for the safety of the citizens and public service
personnel, and for the protection of property. These procedures for emergency response are in
accordance with the National Incident Management System (NIMS) standards and expectations
outlined by the US Department of Homeland Security.

354.02 – 354.08 Unavailable

354.09 GREATER DALLAS/FORT WORTH REGIONAL LAW ENFORCEMENT
         INTERLOCAL ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT
Fort Worth has joined other cities and counties within the North Texas area in the Greater
Dallas/Fort Worth Regional Law Enforcement Interlocal Assistance Agreement. This agreement
allows those signatories to the agreement to call upon one another for support during times of
natural or other disaster, or riot when the situation is such that it cannot be contained by the law
enforcement agency in whose jurisdiction the problem exists.
A. If a crisis does exist in another jurisdiction, and the law enforcement agency in that jurisdiction
    wishes to invoke the provisions of the assistance agreement, the agency involved may contact
    the dispatch supervisor with the details of the request. The Communications Commander will
    be responsible for notifying the Chief of Police, and a decision shall be made as to the level
    of response by the department.
B. If a need arises within Fort Worth requiring the assistance of another jurisdiction’s law
    enforcement personnel and/or equipment, the decision to invoke the provisions of the Greater
    Dallas/Fort Worth Regional Law Enforcement Interlocal Assistance Agreement shall be made
    by the Chief of Police. After the Chief of Police or designee receives a commitment from
    another jurisdiction, instructions shall be passed on to the Police Communications Division
    supervisor for implementation.
C. If assistance through the interlocal agreement is needed for a situation of a non-emergency
    nature including, but not limited to, a request for crime scene personnel and equipment, the
    request shall be forwarded to the unit that would provide the personnel and/or equipment
    requested. The unit supervisor shall advise the Chief of Police of the nature of the request and
    the unit’s capability to respond. The Chief of Police shall make the decision regarding the
    degree of response the department shall be able to provide.
