           409.00        EMPLOYEE COUNSELING AND COACHING
409.01 COMMENDATIONS
A. When a supervisor identifies conduct that merits commendation, the details of the incident
    shall be included in a commendation through Blue Team that will be forwarded up the
    commended officer’s chain of command with a copy issued to the commended officer.
B. Once Internal Affairs receives the commendation from the chain of command, a copy of the
    details provided in the Blue Team Report will be printed on a commendation form and signed
    by the Chief of Police. The commendation will then be sent to the commended officer and a
    copy will be placed in the employee’s permanent personnel file.
C. When commendations are received from outside sources by way of letter, the commended
    officer’s supervisor should initiate a commendation through Blue Team and attach a copy of
    the letter from the outside source.

409.02 VERBAL COUNSELING
 A. Supervisors should handle minor, non-recurring infractions orally with the affected employee.
    This allows supervisors to talk with subordinates about minor issues that don’t require official
    coaching or discipline, and doesn’t require documentation.

                                           305
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


B. Verbal counseling stemming from any Administrative Blue Team Report may be documented
   in the report when no written discipline has been issued.
C. Verbal counseling shall be documented in the Training Development Log located on the portal
   when verbal counseling is the final recommendation on any Administrative Blue Team.

409.03 SUPERVISOR’S COACHING SESSION
A. If the conduct of an officer should require a formal coaching session, a Supervisor’s Coaching
    form shall be used as a means of documenting undesirable work performance or behavior that
    may appear to be a recurring problem.
B. If the undesirable work performance was documented in an accident through Blue Team, the
    Supervisor’s Coaching Session can be issued once approved by the appropriate Division
    Commander or Captain. A Supervisor’s Coaching Session stemming from behavior not
    related to an accident shall be documented in an Administrative Blue Team sent through the
    Chain of Command. The Supervisor’s Coaching Session should only be issued after the
    appropriate Division Commander or Captain has reviewed all documentation and has
    approved the Supervisor’s Coaching Session.
C. The supervisor’s coaching form must include a description of the violation, including date and
    time, witnesses, what is expected from the employee to correct the situation, and subsequent
    actions that may take place if the employee fails to comply.
D. The supervisor, employee, and any other persons present at the supervisor’s coaching session
    must sign the form. The employee may provide written comments regarding the incident under
    separate cover, which must also be signed by all persons involved in the session.
E. The employee shall be given the original copy of the supervisor’s coaching form and the
    supervisor shall upload a copy to the associated Blue Team Administrative Report.
F. A copy of the Supervisor’s Coaching form shall be placed in the employee’s unit file.
G. Supervisor’s Coaching forms shall be removed and destroyed from the unit file after six (6)
    months from issue.

409.04 COMMAND LEVEL COACHING SESSION
A. The Command Level Coaching Session enables a division commander/captain or higher
    authority to deal with inappropriate conduct which is more serious than conduct normally
    addressed in Supervisor’s Coaching Sessions, but does not require a formal Written
    Reprimand.
B. If while reviewing an Administrative Blue Team or Accident Blue Team, a captain or a
    commander identifies inappropriate conduct that merits more formal documentation the
    captain or commander may, with approval of the Deputy Chief, issue a Command Level
    Coaching Session.
C. The Command Level Coaching form shall:
    1. Provide the details of the inappropriate conduct, including the date of occurrence.
    2. List the General Order, procedure, or rule the conduct violated.
    3. Provide a statement that the Command Level Coaching form will be placed in the
        employee’s unit file for twelve (12) months.
    4. Be issued under the Commander/Captain’s signature.
    5. Only be issued by sworn commanders, division captains, or civilian equivalent.
D. The commander/captain shall have the employee sign a copy of the Command Level Coaching
    form. If the officer refuses to sign, it shall be so noted. The employee may provide written

                                          306
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


    comments regarding the incident under separate cover, which must also be signed by all
    persons involved in the session.
    1. The original signed copy shall be given to the employee and a copy attached to the
        associated Blue Team Administrative Report.
    2. The commander/captain shall place a copy of the Command Level Coaching form in the
        employee’s unit file.
    3. Command Level Coaching forms shall be removed and destroyed from the unit file after
        twelve (12) months from issue.

409.05 WRITTEN REPRIMAND
A. A Written Reprimand enables a captain, division commander or higher authority to deal with
    inappropriate conduct which is more serious than conduct normally addressed in a Command
    Level Coaching Session, but does not require a formal discipline.
B. If while reviewing an Administrative Blue Team or Accident Blue Team, a member of the
    department at or above the rank of captain, commander, or higher identifies inappropriate
    conduct that merits more formal documentation, the captain, commander or above may, with
    approval of the Deputy Chief or Assistant Chief issue a Written Reprimand.
C. The Written Reprimand form shall:
    1. Provide the details of the inappropriate conduct, including the date of occurrence.
    2. List the General Order, procedure, or rule the conduct violated.
    3. Provide a statement that the Written Reprimand form will be placed in the employee’s
         permanent personnel file.
    4. Only be issued and signed by sworn member of the police department at or above the
         rank of captain, commander, their civilian equivalent, or higher.
D. The captain, commander or above shall provide the original of the Written Reprimand form
    to the employee.
E. The captain, commander or above shall have the employee sign a copy of the Written
    Reprimand form. If the officer refuses to sign, it shall be so noted. The employee may provide
    written comments regarding the incident under separate cover, which must also be signed by
    the person who issued the reprimand.
    1. The original signed copy shall be given to the employee and a copy attached to the
         associated Blue Team Administrative Report.
    2. A final signed copy of the Written Reprimand shall be placed in the employee’s
         permanent file, along with any written comments provided by the employee.
F. The employee may use the departmental grievance procedure to contest any written reprimand
    which they believe to be unjust.

                    410.00        DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES

410.01 DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES: SCOPE
A. All department employees shall be subject to disciplinary action for acts of misconduct.
B. In reference to civil service employees, misconduct is defined as any act committed or omitted
    as required by the twelve (12) rules listed in General Order 410.02(B). TBP 2.04
C. The Professional Standards Division is designated by the Chief of Police as the official
    repository for all complaints received related to police employees. The Professional Standards
    Division shall provide periodic reports to the Chief regarding the current status of all
                                          307
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


    investigations and shall keep the Chief apprised of any incident resulting in discipline as
    defined in General Order 410.02 (A). TBP 2.06
410.02 DISCIPLINARY ACTION: CIVIL SERVICE EMPLOYEES TBP 2.06
A. The form of disciplinary action for civil service employees may be:
    1. Suspension without pay.
    2. Demotion.
    3. Indefinite suspension.
    4. Termination.
         a. In cases involving a felony conviction.
B. The following twelve (12) rules as set forth in Chapter 143, Local Government Code, and the
    Rules and Regulations of the City of Fort Worth Civil Service Commission, are causes for
    written coachings, reprimands, and/or disciplinary action, including removal or suspension
    for civil service employees.
    1. Conviction of a felony or other crime involving moral turpitude.
         a. Conviction of a felony is cause for termination and conviction of a class A or B
              misdemeanor may be cause for disciplinary action or indefinite suspension. (Chapter
              143, Local Government Code, Section 143.056).
    2. Violation of the provisions of the City of Fort Worth charter.
    3. Acts of incompetency.
    4. Neglect of duty.
    5. Discourtesy to the public or to fellow employee while the officer is in the line of duty.
    6. Acts showing lack of good moral character.
    7. Drinking intoxicants while on-duty or intoxication while off-duty.
    8. Conduct prejudicial to good order.
    9. Refusal or neglect to pay just debts.
    10. Absence without leave.
    11. Shirking duty or cowardice at fires, if applicable.
    12. Violation of any of the rules, regulations, or any orders of the police department.

410.03 DISCIPLINARY ACTION: NON-CIVIL SERVICE PERSONNEL
A. Disciplinary procedures for non-civil service personnel are governed by the City of Fort
    Worth Personnel Rules and Regulations. Supervisors should refer to the Personnel Rules and
    Regulations for General Employees and consult with Police Employment Services when
    taking disciplinary action against a non-sworn employee.

410.04 MANAGING PERSONNEL COMPLAINT
A. Definitions
    1. Personnel complaint - an allegation, received from any source, of misconduct or violation
       of policy by a department employee.
    2. Personnel complaint form - a form completed by Internal Affairs that is signed by the
       complaining or reporting party.
    3. External complaints - any complaint originating from a person who is not a sworn
       employee in the Fort Worth Police Department, including, but not limited to, complaints
       from citizens and complaints from non-sworn City employees.



                                          308
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


    4.Internal complaints - any complaint originating from a sworn employee of the Fort Worth
      Police Department, including misconduct observed or reported by a sworn employee of
      the Fort Worth Police Department.
   5. Complaining Party/Complainant - is a person making a complaint that they were harmed
      by the officer’s alleged misconduct.
   6. Reporting Party - is a person who is a witness or third-party source of information
      regarding alleged misconduct. If the Department initiates a complaint on the basis of
      reported information, a supervisor or Internal Affairs investigator can be the reporting
      party for the complaint.
B. General Information
   1. All complaints against police employees shall be received, investigated, and disposed of
      in accordance with the procedures set forth herein in addition to the City Personnel Rules
      and Regulations, the Meet and Confer Agreement, and Civil Service law, as applicable.
         TBP 2.06
    2.   Fort Worth Police Department personnel shall inform any person who wishes to make a
         complaint against a police officer or police department employee of the existence of the
         formal complaint procedure and, without unnecessary delay, contact and refer such
         persons to a police field supervisor, Internal Affairs, or the Police Oversight Monitor. TBP
         2.04
    3. All personnel complaints shall be accepted and all Personnel Complaint forms shall be
       completed by Internal Affairs without unnecessary delay whenever: TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06
       a. The complaint is of misconduct of a nature which, if true, would normally result in
            a form of disciplinary action outlined in General Order 410.02.
       b. The complaint is received from a source outside the department, i.e., citizen
            complaint, or the alleged violation involves an incident of serious nature.
    4. A Personnel Complaint form shall not be completed when complaints are solely about
       department policies or procedures, as opposed to conduct in violation of a policy or
       procedure. If a complaint is determined to concern department policies or procedures and
       no misconduct is indicated, and the incident cannot be explained to the complaining
       person’s satisfaction, that person shall be referred to the organizational entity having
       administrative control over the subject matter. TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06
    5. A reporting supervisor shall not have the responsibility of generating a Personnel
       Complaint Form. Internal Affairs will generate all Personnel Complaint forms. TBP 2.04
    6. Personnel Complaint forms shall be witnessed when an allegation of misconduct is
       received from a source other than sworn personnel. In instances where a valid reason
       exists for not obtaining the reporting party’s signature, the signature of the Internal Affairs
       investigator in the “Reporting Party” block will be considered a valid substitute for the
       signature of the reporting party.
    7. A supervisor shall not conduct an investigation of alleged misconduct if they are the
        complaining party, the ultimate decision-maker regarding disciplinary action, or if they
        have any personal involvement regarding the alleged misconduct. In such instances, the
        supervisor will report the event to their immediate supervisor who will either obtain
        preliminary information regarding the complaint and generate a Blue Team with attached
        information, or assign another supervisor to do so. (If the employee finds it
        uncomfortable to report an issue to their immediate supervisor, then they can follow the
        procedures outlined in G.O. 205.01 (B)(1)). The Blue Team will then be forwarded:
       a. Directly to Internal Affairs if the complaint is received from citizen or non-sworn
            personnel; or
                                           309
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


         b.Through the chain of command to the Division Commander/Captain if an internal or
           administrative complaint.
C. When an external complaint, e.g., citizen complaint, is received by Communications/Field
   Supervision (29CCO):
   1.   Supervisor call shall be generated and be dispatched to the appropriate field sergeant.
   2.   The call taker should only obtain the complaining party’s name, phone number, and the
        officer about whom they are making a complaint. Under no circumstances are Call
        Takers, Dispatchers, or Dispatch Supervisors to screen or discourage callers who wish
        to make a complaint against a police officer/employee from doing so.
   3.   The sergeant/supervisor’s unit number shall be the only information placed in the CAD
        details rather than the officer’s name.
   4.   Whenever possible, the call should be dispatched to the officer’s direct supervisor. If
        the supervisor is unavailable, then it should be dispatched to a sergeant on the same
        patrol team. As a last resort, it should be dispatched to any supervisor within the same
        division.
D. Procedure for Investigating Complaints
   1. For external complaints:
       a. Without discouraging the complaining party from making a complaint, the
           responding supervisor will, to the best of their ability, obtain the nature of the alleged
           violation, and initiate a Blue Team incident, if warranted.
       b. The responding supervisor shall meet in person with the complainant. If the
           supervisor is unable to meet with the person or will be delayed for a substantial
           amount of time due to other duties, the supervisor shall contact another supervisor to
           meet with the person. A supervisor may contact the complainant by phone if the
           complainant has left the original call location and is several miles beyond the city
           limits of Fort Worth. Unless exigent circumstances exist, supervisors shall personally
           meet with complainant. The responding supervisor shall capture the interaction on
           their body-worn camera or in-car video, and document the interaction and tag the
           video accordingly.
       c. The supervisor shall initiate a “Personnel Complaint -Sworn” incident on Blue Team
           with the details conveyed to the supervisor by the complaining party and shall
           forward the Blue Team to Internal Affairs within 24 hours.
           (1) If the complaint merely poses questions on department practice and policy:
                 (a) The supervisor will document the result of the investigation in the call
                     disposition.
                 (b) The body-worn camera and/or in-car video will be uploaded to
                     Evidence.com.
       d. When a personnel complaint is received from a third-party source, the information
           should be documented by the field supervisor, attached to a Blue Team, and
           forwarded directly to Internal Affairs. The third-party source shall be asked to sign
           the Personnel Complaint form, generated by Internal Affairs as the reporting party.
           Unless the personnel complaint is validated by subsequent interview of an actual
           party to the incident, the final disposition of such complaint shall not be listed on an
           officer’s Internal Affairs record. All reports related to such complaints shall be filed
           as miscellaneous memorandums by Internal Affairs.
       e. When a personnel complaint is received from an intoxicated person, the information
           should be documented by the field supervisor, attached to a Blue Team, and
                                            310
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


              forwarded directly to Internal Affairs. The complaining person shall be re-
              interviewed by Internal Affairs at the earliest opportunity after having regained
              sobriety. During the re-interview, the complaining person shall be asked to sign the
              Personnel Complaint form, generated by Internal Affairs. Unless the personnel
              complaint is validated by subsequent interview of the intoxicated person, the final
              disposition of such complaint shall not be listed on an officer’s Internal Affairs
              record. All reports related to such complaints shall be filed as miscellaneous
              memorandums by Internal Affairs.
    2.   For internal complaints:
         a. When any supervisor becomes aware of possible misconduct, either through personal
              observation or other means, except for complaints received from external sources as
              described in the previous section, the supervisor shall take action to prevent
              continuation or aggravation of the incident. The supervisor shall also conduct a
              preliminary investigation, which shall include, when applicable:
              (1) Names, identification numbers, and assignments of all involved employees,
                   including employees who are witnesses.
              (2) Names, addresses and telephone numbers of the complaining person and any
                   known witnesses to the incident who are not department employees. Times,
                   locations, and business and residential telephone numbers where these
                   individuals may be contacted shall be indicated.
              (3) A statement from the complaining person obtained by an interview of that person
                   by the reporting supervisor.
              (4) Photographs of actual or claimed injuries to the complaining person.
              (5) Photographs shall be taken in all cases involving allegations of excessive force.
              (6) Any available information regarding medical treatment obtained by the
                   complaining person as a result of the incident.
             (7) The disposition of any evidence obtained.
         b. Minor policy violations or Coaching issues that will not reflect discredit upon the
              department, but which indicate a need for some form of corrective action and/or
              training, may be dealt with by the involved officer’s immediate supervisor with the
              review and concurrence of the involved employee’s division commander/captain. TBP
             2.04 and TBP 2.06
             (1) Coaching Issues are minor, internal department issues requiring supervisory
                 coaching above the level of verbal coaching, but not arising to the level of a
                 Written Reprimand. These are clear-cut issues not requiring a personnel
                 complaint or an Internal Affairs investigation. Examples would include
                 reoccurrences of not activating camera, late for roll call, etc. The determination
                 of the handling of these issues at the unit level would be at the discretion of the
                 Commander/Captain of the Division.
             (2) With Division Commander/Captain approval documented on Blue Team, the
                 supervisor of appropriate rank may issue a Supervisor’s Coaching or Captain’s
                 Coaching form, generate and attach the form to the appropriate Blue Team, and
                 forward the Blue Team directly to the Internal Affairs. This will NOT apply to
                 citizen or non-sworn initiated complaints.
                 (a) A copy of the completed coaching form will be attached or documented
                      on the Blue Team and forwarded to Internal Affairs within two (2) weeks.


                                           311
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


              (3) If the Commander/Captain determines that the investigation could result in
                  discipline as defined under General Order 410.02 A (i.e., suspension, demotion,
                  indefinite suspension, or termination), the Division Commander/Captain shall
                  forward the investigation to Internal Affairs within four (4) days of receipt of
                  the Blue Team.
   3. Division commanders/captains have the primary responsibility for investigating
        personnel complaints made against employees of their divisions. A division
        commander/captain who becomes aware of any allegation of misconduct shall monitor
        all resulting activities and shall ensure that personnel under their command have fulfilled
        their responsibilities provided in this order. A division commander/captain may request
        that Internal Affairs conduct an investigation on any allegation of misconduct or
        personnel complaint. TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06
E. Complaints from anonymous sources
   1. A Personnel Complaint form shall not be completed for personnel complaints received
        from anonymous sources; however, when information is received by a supervisor which
        originated from an anonymous source, the supervisor shall complete a Blue Team
        detailing the information received and forward it to Internal Affairs. TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06
   2. If the information received is of a nature that would jeopardize the integrity of an
        investigation by being reduced to writing, it shall be handled in accordance with General
        Order 410.05.
   3. If the information received describes misconduct of a nature which, if true, would
        normally result in a form of disciplinary action outlined in General Order 410.02, a
        preliminary investigation will be conducted by Internal Affairs.
   4. When warranted, the allegation of misconduct shall be reported on a Personnel Complaint
        form. If the identity of the anonymous reporting party cannot be determined or the
        reporting party, if identified, refuses to sign the Personnel Complaint form, the signature
        of the Internal Affairs investigator in the “Reporting Party” block will be considered a
        valid substitute for the signature of the reporting party. TBP 2.04
F. When an employee other than a supervisor is made aware of a complaint either through
   personal observation or other means, of possible misconduct they shall, if applicable, take
   corrective action to preclude continuation or escalation of the incident and shall immediately
   notify a supervisor. TBP 2.04

410.05 DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES: SENSITIVE INVESTIGATION
A. When a personnel complaint or incident is of a nature that the integrity of the investigation
    may be compromised or jeopardized by reducing the incident to writing, the reporting
    supervisor shall immediately report the incident to their lieutenant, who shall report said
    incident to the lieutenant of Internal Affairs.
B. If the reporting supervisor has reason to believe the integrity of the investigation may be
    compromised by passage through normal channels, the supervisor shall personally report the
    incident directly to the lieutenant of Internal Affairs. TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06
C. When immediate action is required or the seriousness of the incident is such that it may subject
    the department to severe criticism or liability, the reporting supervisor shall provide
    immediate notification to the involved employee’s division commander/captain and to the
    Captain of the Professional Standards Division. If after hours, this notification shall be made
    through a callback notification through the Communications Division. TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06

                                           312
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


    1.   In incidents of this magnitude, the Chief of Police or the appropriate Bureau Assistant
         Chief may place the involved employee on Restricted or Detached duty, with pay, and
         shall, when applicable, take custody of the employee’s badge, identification card, and
         service weapon (unless personally owned).
    2.   If the decision is made to place an officer on restricted or detached duty, Internal Affairs
         shall be contacted to facilitate the process, complete required documentation, and take
         custody of the involved employees’ badge, commission card, and service weapon (unless
         personally owned).
    3.   The reinstatement of the officer and return of equipment can only be authorized by the
         affected officer’s bureau Assistant Chief.

410.06 DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES: INTERNAL AFFAIRS RESPONSIBILITIES
A. The lieutenant or above of Internal Affairs shall act in a staff advisory capacity when
    necessary. The Internal Affairs Lieutenant may assume responsibility for the investigation of
    any personnel complaint when, in the opinion of the lieutenant, it is advisable to do so. The
    lieutenant also has the authority to obtain the advice and assistance of any departmental entity.
B. Internal Affairs shall assume responsibility for an internal or external personnel complaint
    designated as a Tier One Investigation. An investigation is classified as Tier One when:
    1. It has been alleged an employee has committed any felony or Class A or B misdemeanor.
    2. The allegation of misconduct is against employees of more than one division.
    3. The investigation involves an allegation of:
         (a) Excessive force,
         (b) Sexual harassment or inappropriate conduct of a sexual nature,
         (c) Hostile work environment,
         (d) Disparate treatment or inappropriate comment due to gender, race, ethnicity, age, or
              sexual orientation,
         (e) Retaliation for reporting the misconduct of another, or
         (f) Untruthfulness.
    4. The allegations have attracted media attention.
    5. The Internal Affairs Lieutenant determines it is in the Department’s best interest.
C. Tier Two Investigations will consist of cases not falling under the above criteria. Internal
    Affairs will assume responsibility for all Tier Two Investigations which involve one of the
    following:
    1. Any complaint received from citizen or non-sworn personnel not meeting Tier One
         criteria.
    2. Internal complaint designated for investigation following consultation with a Captain or
         Commander over a division that will likely result in discipline as defined under General
         Order 410.02 A (i.e., suspension, demotion, indefinite suspension, or termination).
    3. Cases as determined by the Internal Affairs Lieutenant or the Internal Affairs
         Administrative Sergeant
D. The Internal Affairs investigator or supervisor performing the investigation shall provide the
    employee with the written allegations in the complaint no less than 48 hours before the initial
    interview or requesting any inter-office correspondence or other correspondence related to the
    incident from the employee. TBP 2.04 and TBP 2.06
NOTE: The 48-hour notice does not apply to on-scene investigations that occur immediately after
    an incident.

Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


410.07 ARRESTED DEPARTMENTAL EMPLOYEE
A. If an employee of the department is detained or arrested for any criminal offense within the
    City of Fort Worth, the officer detaining or arresting the employee shall immediately notify a
    supervisor of the division in which the employee is detained or arrested.
B. A supervisor who has been notified that an employee of the department has been arrested or
    detained shall immediately proceed to the scene and shall ensure that a lieutenant or above of
    the patrol division in which the incident occurs is immediately notified.
C. The lieutenant of the patrol division shall ensure immediate notification is made to:
    1. The Internal Affairs lieutenant.
    2. Special Investigations personnel.
    3. The commander/captain of the employee’s division of assignment.
    4. The Public Information Officer.
D. Internal Affairs shall conduct an investigation whenever an employee is arrested for or
    believed to be a principal suspect in a felony or class A or B misdemeanor offense. When
    warranted, Special Investigations personnel shall be responsible for submitting the criminal
    case to the District Attorney for consideration of criminal prosecution. The Captain of the
    Professional Standards Division has the discretion to assume responsibility for investigations
    related to class C misdemeanor violations.
E. When any employee of the department is detained or becomes aware that they are believed to
    be the principal suspect in a criminal offense, other than minor traffic violations committed
    outside the City of Fort Worth, including offenses committed outside of the State of Texas,
    the employee shall as soon as possible notify a supervisor.
    1. All employees of the department must notify a supervisor as soon as possible regarding
         any changes, corrections, or updates to criminal charges, including criminal convictions
         for offenses other than minor traffic violations, within the employee’s criminal history
         report.
F. When any employee of the department becomes aware that another employee has been
    detained or is believed to be a principal actor in a criminal offense, other than minor traffic
    violations committed outside the city, the employee shall immediately notify a supervisor.
G. Any supervisor who is notified regarding the detainment or arrest of an employee by another
    law enforcement agency, other than minor traffic violations, shall ensure that immediate
    notification is made to Internal Affairs and to the division commander of the involved
    employee.
H. Internal Affairs personnel shall respond to the scene or to the indicated outside agency when
    the incident involves an alleged felony or class A or B misdemeanor.
    1. A supervisor from the involved employee’s division of assignment shall respond on
         alleged class C misdemeanor violations if the violation is of a magnitude to require
         immediate investigation.
         a. Regardless of whether a supervisor responds to the scene, a Personnel Complaint
              form shall still be prepared and processed.
    2. The responding supervisor shall conduct a preliminary investigation and a Personnel
         Complaint form shall be prepared and processed as described in General Order 410.06.
    3. The responding supervisor shall advise concerned members of the outside agency that
         the preliminary investigation is for internal administrative purposes only and that any
         evidence obtained by the responding supervisor solely as a result of interviewing the
         involved employee shall not be disclosed to the agency conducting the criminal

                                           314
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


         investigation. Responding supervisors shall exercise extreme care not to interfere with
         the investigation of the outside agency.

410.08 DISPOSITION OF ADMINISTRATIVE INVESTIGATIONS
A. Administrative investigations which may result in disciplinary action shall be completed
    within thirty (30) calendar days from the date the complaint is received or initiated. TBP 2.05
    Note: Due to the complicated nature of some investigations, the investigation deadline may
              be extended by the Operational Command Deputy Chief.
B. Unless approved by the Chief of Police or designee, the complete administrative investigation
    review, employee notification, and issuance of any discipline will be the responsibility of the
    chain of command of the officer at the time of the incident or misconduct. If an employee is
    moved prior to the completion of the investigation, the chain-of-command responsible for that
    employee at the time the incident occurred will continue the investigation, review and
    notifications. Reassignment of the officer does not reassign responsibility of any part of the
    investigative, notification or discipline process.
C. The review by the chain of command shall be completed within twenty-one (21) calendar days
    of the date the investigation is completed or the date the investigative report is received from
    Internal Affairs. The chain of command may receive an extension with approval from the
    Chief of Police. TBP 2.05
D. Internal Affairs shall submit the completed investigation to the involved employee’s
    Commander/Captain. The Commander/Captain will designate a Lieutenant to review the case
    (depending on the rank of the involved employee this can differ). Example: involved
    employee is a Lieutenant, the case will be sent to the Deputy Chief, who will designate a
    Commander/Captain to review the case). This person shall:
    1. Prepare a summary report using the “Field Write-up” template provided on the internal
       police department portal. This report will have findings for each allegation and, if
       necessary, make a recommendation for discipline. Each allegation will be resolved with
       one of the following dispositions:
       a.     Unfounded: The investigation reveals sufficient evidence to believe the complained
              of act did not occur.
       b.     Exonerated: The investigation reveals the complained of act occurred but was legal,
              proper, and justified.
       c.     Not-Sustained: The investigation discloses insufficient evidence to believe the
              complained of act either did or did not occur.
       d.     Sustained: The investigation discloses sufficient evidence to conclude the
              complained of act occurred.
    2. Discuss the findings with the involved officer’s sergeant (or applicable rank depending
         on the rank of the involved employee) to determine an appropriate discipline
         recommendation,
    3. Discuss the findings and recommendation for disciplinary action with the involved
         employee in person, documenting the meeting in the summary report, and
    4. Forward the completed investigation and summary report for review to the next level in
         the chain of command.
E. When a completed investigation is forwarded for review, the next higher level will meet with
    the preceding level to discuss the disciplinary recommendations. Each ascending level shall
    document the results of that meeting as follows:

                                           315
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


     1.   If the next level up concurs with the lower-level findings, they will document concurrence
          in the comments section of the Blue Team report. No additional IOC is necessary.
     2. If the next level up disagrees with the lower-level finding, the higher level will generate
          and attach a new IOC to document their explanation for disagreement, their findings, and
          their recommendations.
     3. Once they complete their findings, each level of the chain that provides a recommendation
          for discipline should meet with the officer to give their recommendation.
F.   The review process will continue moving through ascending levels in the chain of command
     until it reaches one level above the designated permissible discipline levels established by the
     Meet & Confer contract in effect at the time the misconduct occurred.
     Example: If the conduct occurred during 2018, and the recommended discipline is a three (3)-
     day suspension or less, then a commander would issue the discipline and notate in the
     BlueTeam comments which deputy chief concurred with the discipline.
G.   Disciplinary suspensions may only be served by the rank of commander and above. Captains
     and below are not permitted to issue a disciplinary suspension. Meetings between the
     appointed rank and the officer for all disciplinary suspensions shall be scheduled by the
     appointed rank and held in the office of Internal Affairs or an agreed upon location. Internal
     Affairs personnel will assist the appointed rank by generating the appropriate paperwork for
     the meeting.
H.   Upon completion of the review and issuance of discipline, the final reviewer shall forward the
     investigation and all related documents to Internal Affairs.
I.   Under no circumstances shall any level of review change or require a change in conclusions
     and/or recommendations of another.
J.   If any level of review determines that additional investigation is required, the further
     investigation shall normally be conducted by the supervisor or Internal Affairs investigator
     conducting the original investigation.
K.   When an investigation subsequently discloses additional allegations of misconduct which
     were not described in the original personnel complaint, and the classification of the original
     complaint is other than sustained, a new complaint form shall be prepared and a supplemental
     investigative report completed. When any allegation of misconduct in the original personnel
     complaint is sustained, the new allegations may be recorded as separate supplemental charges
     in the investigative report for the original complaint.

                         411.00        MEDIATION PROGRAM

411.01 MEDIATION PROGRAM
The Fort Worth Police Department through the mediation process, seeks to enhance
communications between and restore the interests of the involved parties while also addressing the
community member's complaint against the officer in a timely, fair, and equitable manner.

411.02 DEFINITIONS
A. Ineligible Issue - An issue is ineligible for the mediation process if it can be described as a
    significant policy violation or if it is so egregious that it threatens the integrity of the Fort
    Worth Police Department (e.g., deadly force or civil rights violations). An issue may be
    ineligible for mediation if the nature or magnitude of the issue makes it impractical for

                                            316
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


     mediation. Certain management decisions, discipline, or policy issues shall not be eligible for
     mediation.
B.   Involved Parties - The phrase used to describe collectively the complainant and officer.
C.   Mediation - A forum in which an impartial person, the mediator, facilitates communication
     between parties to promote understanding and reconciliation that may result in a resolution.
D.   Mediation Procedure - The term used to describe all mediation-related activities collectively,
     including intake, education, interviews, mediation sessions, evaluations, and file closure.
E.   Mediation Session - The mediation meeting wherein the parties and the mediator assemble in
     private to discuss issues of concern.
F.   Mediator - An individual who has completed a minimum of forty-five (45) hours of mediation
     training and is selected to act as a neutral participant during a mediation session to facilitate
     the discussion.
G.   Participant - Any party who has a role in the mediation procedure including any interview,
     training, or meeting.
H.   Party - Any person having an interest in an issue or concern forwarded to the Office of Police
     Oversight Monitor (OPOM) or Fort Worth Police Department for mediation.
I.   Support Person - The complainant and the Fort Worth Police Department member may each
     bring an individual as a Support Person to the mediation. This individual will not participate
     in the mediation except to observe and provide support. If that individual is an adult
     accompanying a minor, or was present at the time of the if the incident, they may participate
     in the mediation.

411.03 MEDIATION PROCESS
A. When a complaint is received by the Office of Police Oversight Monitor (OPOM) or the Fort
    Worth Police Department, Internal Affairs will assess whether the officer is eligible to
    participate in the mediation procedure. If eligible and the complainant is determined to be
    eligible by OPOM and the complainant agrees, an offer to mediate will be extended to the
    officer.
    1. The officer may not be eligible to participate in mediation if:
         a. The officer has displayed a similar pattern of the accused behavior within the past
              year, or
         b. The officer has participated in mediation more than three (3) times that year.
    2. OPOM and Internal Affairs shall review referred complaints to ensure that they are
         eligible for mediation. Internal Affairs will classify the complaint and review the officer’s
         complaint history to determine if the officer is eligible for mediation. FWPD’s issues
         ineligible for mediation may include:
         a. A complaint contains multiple allegations against officer,
         b. Officer’s complaint history, and
         c. Officer’s disciplinary history.
B. Although the majority of allegations list below are policy violations, allegations that may be
    considered eligible for mediation include, but are not limited to, the following:
    1. Denial of medical treatment
    2. Discourtesy
    3. Failure to make a report
    4. Failure to take police action
    5. Failure to perform duties
    6. Inappropriate comments
                                            317
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


     7. Inappropriate gesture
     8. Profane language
     9. Rudeness
     10. Unprofessional attitude/conduct/criticism
     11. Untimely/failure to submit/make a report
     12. Failure to investigate thoroughly
C.   After determination of eligibility and their agreement, OPOM will contact the involved parties
     to begin the mediation procedure.
     1. Officers shall cooperate with OPOM personnel in scheduling mediation meetings and
          throughout the mediation process. Officers who fail to adhere to these requirements will
          have their complaint returned to Internal Affairs to facilitate the normal investigative
          process.
          a. If the involved officer is going to be late for the scheduled mediation, they should
               contact the OPOM immediately to inform them what time they will arrive.
          b. If the involved officer is unable to attend the mediation due to an unforeseen
               emergency, they should make every reasonable effort to immediately notify OPOM
               in order to reschedule the session. The OPOM will contact Internal Affairs to
               determine if there was a legitimate reason for the officer’s failure to attend the
               mediation session.
          c. Unless extenuating circumstances, if the officer fails to attend, the complaint will be
               fully investigated by Internal Affairs.
     2. Officers shall wear their city-issued uniform or professional business attire for the
          scheduled mediation session.
D.   A mediator will be chosen from a random pool of volunteer mediators. Unless there are
     extenuating circumstances, mediation shall occur within thirty (30) calendar days of
     acceptance by the parties and selection of a mediator.
E.   If the involved parties decline to participate in the mediation process at any time, then the case
     will be resolved through the standard investigative process.
F.   Complaints eligible for resolution through mediation shall be processed and completed within
     forty-five (45) calendar days from the date the complaint was approved for the mediation
     procedure unless extenuating circumstances.
G.   All proceedings in the course of mediation shall remain confidential. No employee or officer
     may disclose any confidential information related to the involved parties’ mediation procedure
     or session or engage in any investigative or prosecuting function arising out of a complaint in
     which such person has acted on behalf of the agency.
H.   The mediation procedure is not punitive and involved parties shall not be penalized or
     disciplined for participating. However, mediation cannot shield officers from an investigation
     of a violation of the law, for any allegation not mediated, or for any allegation not eligible to
     be resolved by the mediation process.
I.   Any violation of the confidentiality laws, regulations and policies, or act of retaliation related
     to mediation shall be investigated according to City of Fort Worth and/or Fort Worth Police
     Department regulations, and employees and officers may be subject to disciplinary action.

411.04 MEDIATION RESULTS
A. Both parties are required to participate in good faith in the mediation session. Agreements are
    totally voluntary, but not required, and when applicable, must be agreed to by both parties.
B. Failure to reach an agreement has no impact on any later consideration of the complaint.
                                             318
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


C. Issues addressed by reconciliation using the mediation process are closed and noted as
   “Mediated.”

                412.00        POLICE OFFICERS’ BILL OF RIGHTS
412.01 POLICE OFFICERS’ BILL OF RIGHTS
A. Contacts
    1. An investigator shall make every attempt to contact the employee at a reasonable time
         and place, and to conduct the interview during the employee’s normal tour of duty.
    2. If the employee is caused to return to duty for the purpose of any interview, the city shall
         be required to compensate the employee at the current compensation rate in effect for
         call-back.
B. Telephone Interviews
    Interviews held by telephone must indicate the person interviewing the employee, the time,
    place, and date, which must be reasonable, and the nature of the allegations or act. If the
    investigator reduces the recording to writing, the employees involved shall be furnished upon
    request with an accurate transcript of the conversation which they in turn must proofread for
    error and then sign under the seal of a notary.
C. Investigations and Polygraph Examinations
    1. Employees shall be entitled to all legal rights including:
         a. Notice of allegation.
              (1) The involved employee shall be given a copy of the Personnel Complaint form
                   signed by the reporting party and/or the supervisor who completed the form,
                   within a reasonable time after the complaint is filed. A “reasonable time” is
                   generally to be interpreted as 48 hours before the employee’s investigative
                   interview; however, this does not apply to an investigation that takes place
                   immediately after an incident occurs. In such instances, the involved employee
                   shall be furnished with a copy of the Personnel Complaint form as soon as
                   practicable.
              (2) A sign back receipt shall be required when the involved employee receives a
                   copy of the Personnel Complaint form.
         b. Nature of charges either criminal, civil, or administrative.
         c. Appropriate constitutional warning, in the case of a criminal investigation, and the
              appropriate internal warning, in the case of an administrative investigation.
         d. Allowed to review, but not copy verbatim, photocopy or photograph, any information
              collected during the course of an administrative investigation. The investigator shall
              determine at what point in the investigation the Officer shall be allowed this review,
              however, once the Officer receives a written statement of suspension related to the
              investigation, the Officer and his or her counsel shall be provided a copy of the
              complete investigation, to the extent authorized by law, no later than five (5) days
              after the Officer receives the written statement of suspension.
         e. Right to advice by counsel outside of the interview.
    2. The investigator shall inform the employee whether they are being interviewed as a
         witness or an involved party.
    3. If at any time the nature of the investigation encompasses criminal matter where the
         officer could be criminally charged, the employee shall be informed they are being

                                           319
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


          interviewed as a suspect, and shall have the right to constitutional warning, privilege
          against self-incrimination, and right to counsel.
     4. The employee shall enjoy reasonable freedoms during the investigation, including
          smoking, drinking, restroom privileges, and telephone calls.
     5. The investigator shall in no way subject the employee to harsh, abusive language or
          humiliating treatment and if said treatment occurs, the exception shall be recorded in the
          interview record.
     6. Interviews must be related to the act alleged.
     7. The employee must answer all questions truthfully and not withhold any pertinent
          information.
     8. Any employee attempting to influence or interfere with an investigative action, other than
          through prescribed channels, shall be subject to disciplinary action.
     9. In investigative actions where citizens of the community are contacted as to the character
          of the employee at the request of the employee being investigated, it shall be the
          responsibility of the investigator instituting such interviews to recontact the citizen and
          advise them of the outcome of the investigation.
     10. The Chief of Police has the authority to require an employee to take a polygraph for the
          purposes of an investigation.
     11. Employees shall not be required to sign any document indicating that they were not under
          duress when undergoing a polygraph examination at the direction of the Chief of Police.
     12. In polygraph examinations, except for preliminary control questions, questions must be
          specifically addressed to the particular allegations charged in the original investigation.
     13. Any information concerning the acts shall not be made available to any Civil Service
          Commission or appeal board if that information was obtained under false pretenses.
     14. Employees shall have the right to know if their Internal Affairs interview is being
          recorded. They shall also:
          a. Have the right to bring their own recording device to the interview.
          b. Both parties must be aware of all recordings.
          c. The device must be in full sight.
          d. If the recorded interview is to be used in an Internal Affairs case investigation, it may
               be reduced to writing.
          e. If the employee requests a copy of their transcript:
               (1) The employee shall be furnished with a transcript of their interview.
               (2) They must initial the transcript for error.
               (3) Said employees must sign the transcript under the seal of a notary.
     15. All Internal Affairs investigations shall be used exclusively by administration and shall
          not be released to outside agencies without the permission of the Chief of Police.
D. Right to Counsel
All employees shall have the right to free counsel when civil suits are instigated against them as a
result of a situation arising out of the normal duties required by their position, providing they are
acting within the scope of their assignment.

                       415.00         WORKPLACE SITUATIONS

415.01 CHILDREN IN THE WORKPLACE
In rare cases, it may be necessary for employees to bring their children to the worksite during
regular work hours for short periods of time. In such instances, this period of time should not
exceed one (1) hour.
A. Circumstances which may warrant the presence of children at the workplace during regular
    work hours may include, but may not be limited to:
    1. A breakdown of child care arrangements,
    2. Before or after scheduled doctor appointments, or
    3. Brief visitation of parent’s workplace and to meet coworkers.
B. When circumstances might warrant the presence of children in the workplace, the following
    guidelines should be followed:
    1. Prior approval must be obtained from the supervisor.
    2. Children must be escorted and supervised at all times.
    3. For safety reasons, children shall be prohibited from having access to office equipment
        (e.g., shredders, paper cutters, printers, copiers, etc.), fitness equipment (unless part of a
        departmentally-approved and supervised youth program or activity), hazardous material
        areas, areas requiring security clearance, and areas requiring specific safety training,
        equipment or clothing.
    4. Children will not be permitted in public service areas, field, or patrol operations.
    5. Children will not be permitted to ride in city vehicles.
    6. Employees are responsible for the actions of their children. If the child is disruptive, the
        employee will be asked to take the child out of the workplace.
    7. Children with contagious, or potentially contagious, illnesses are not allowed at the
        workplace.
C. A Deputy Chief, Assistant Director, or their designee may set additional guidelines to conform
    with the operations at a particular location or facility.
D. Upon approval, a Deputy Chief, Assistant Director, or their designee may permit employees
    to participate in “Take Your Child to Work” day events and may limit or prohibit such events
    at specific sites or facilities.
E. Permission to bring a child to work is a privilege, not a right or entitlement. Deputy Chiefs,
    Assistant Directors, or their designees shall make decisions in the best interest of the
    organization regarding bringing children into a workplace and these decisions are final.

              416.00        USE OF TRAINING CENTER FACILITIES
416.01 USE OF TRAINING CENTER FACILITIES
A. The Police Training Academy shall be open from 0730 to 1700, Monday through Friday,
    remaining closed on weekends and holidays unless special provisions are made. First priority
    for the use of the facilities shall remain official police department training. In situations of a
    police department mission-critical function, police personnel will have priority over any non-
    critical group that has scheduled use of the training facilities.
B. During those times when the gymnasium and weight room are not in official use for approved
    training by the police department, other organized activities or individual use may be
                                            321
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


   scheduled by contacting the Police Training Division Captain or designee, who shall have full
   authority and responsibility for scheduling. When using the training center after normal hours,
   it shall be the responsibility of each person to verify that any doors used in the building by the
   person and/or their group are secured.
C. Use of the training center gymnasium and weight room shall be limited to police employees,
   both sworn and civilian. No individual or group activities shall be allowed involving non-city
   employees, unless prior written approval is obtained from the Training Captain. Employees
   are strictly prohibited from loaning ID cards to family, friends, or associates for access to the
   facility or controlled areas.
D. Any organization, other than Fort Worth Police or Fire Departments, requesting use of the
   Training Division building will be required to sign a release form.
E. Employees are strictly prohibited from bypassing security systems in the Training Center.
   Bypassing security may include, but not be limited to, tampering with or making an electronic
   door lock or electronic gate inoperable, bypassing the card reader, circumventing settings or
   programing by tampering with the on/off switch, parking on the gate sensor to keep the gate
   open, and/or bracing open an exterior access or an exit-only door or gate which is scheduled
   to be locked.
   NOTE: An exception to bracing open a door for training or other legitimate purposes requires
              advanced authorization from the Training Captain.


                                   417.00         RESERVED

                        418.00        SENIORITY PROCEDURES

418.01 SENIORITY PROCEDURES
A. The Fort Worth Police Department subscribes to the following values and philosophies
    concerning personnel assignments:
    1. Public safety is our primary concern.
    2. The department’s goal is to place the best qualified officer in each position; therefore,
        qualification is the first consideration for assignment.
    3. Civil service rules and procedures determine qualifications for advancement from rank to
        rank.
    4. Management retains the right to set job requirements, make assignments, and exercise
        judgments within the civil service framework; however, management must be prepared
        to explain its decisions.
    5. Seniority is rewarded by the provisions for longevity pay.
    6. Seniority may be considered for personnel assignments of officers below the rank of
        lieutenant.
    7. Special needs or hardships of individual officers may be considered when making
        assignments.
    8. The decisions of the Chief of Police on transfers and/or assignments are not subject to the
        grievance procedure.
B. Assignment for all officers will normally be determined by the following factors:
    1. Special skills or experiences required by the job.
    2. Special training or educational requirements.
                                            322
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


   3. Previous job performance.
   4. Special needs or hardships of individual officers.
C. Normally, seniority for the purpose of asserting a seniority preference, shall be determined by
   the date of commission or promotion to the present rank. If the date of promotion or
   commission are identical for two or more officers, seniority will be determined by officers’
   final position in their graduating academy class or on their promotional list.
   1. Seniority for officers who have received a demotion due to a reduction in force shall be
        determined by the date of original appointment to the rank to which they are being
        demoted.
   2. Seniority for officers who are involuntarily demoted under provisions of chapter 143 of
        the Texas Local Government Code shall be determined by the effective date of the
        demotion.
   3. Seniority for officers who are reappointed after voluntary resignation shall be determined
        by their date of reappointment.
D. Officers in the rank of lieutenant and above may not assert seniority preference for unit
   assignment, shift assignment, days off, vacation leave, or holiday leave. These are
   discretionary personnel decisions made by the Chief of Police in the best interests of the
   department with consideration for any special needs or hardships of individual officers.
E. Officers below the rank of lieutenant may assert seniority preference within their work unit
   for:
   1. Vacation preference.
   2. Days off preferences by work unit as soon as the days become available.
   3. Officers may not bump other officers from their days off, previously set vacation, or other
        scheduled leave because of seniority. This includes officers who have transferred to a
        new unit. However, at the first day off vacancy, etc., that becomes available, the senior
        officer may assert their seniority preference.
   NOTE: Unit shall mean a first line supervisor’s work group.
F. Holiday deployment shall follow the normal course of days off except in those instances when
   increased or reduced deployment is mandated by the circumstances of the holiday.
   Commanders and supervisors shall endeavor to keep holiday deployment at the minimum
   necessary to provide adequate police service.


                                  419.00         RESERVED


    420.00       VACATION, COMPENSATORY, AND HOLIDAY LEAVE
420.01 VACATION LEAVE
A. All division commanders/captains/division managers are responsible for scheduling vacation
    leave on an annual basis for all members of their command/supervision and shall maintain the
    vacation schedule for one (1) full calendar year.
B. Officers shall sign up for vacations by seniority within their units.
C. In cases of transfers, emergencies, or employees with less than one (1) year of continuous
    employment, supervisors shall render decisions which reflect consideration of the employee’s
    problem, but which are in the best interests of the department. In no instance shall an officer
    be allowed to use unearned time.
                                           323
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


D. It shall be the responsibility of supervisors to monitor vacation and holiday time to avoid
   abuse. Additionally, the supervisor shall ensure appropriate staffing before approval of
   vacation leave.

420.02 COMPENSATORY AND HOLIDAY LEAVE
A. Compensatory and accumulated holiday leave may be used in hourly increments.
B. Employees shall request use of compensatory and holiday leave in advance whenever
    possible.
    1. Accumulated compensatory time may be used when the employee desires to use the time,
         if the supervisor agrees the time off may be scheduled at that time.
    2. Supervisors shall grant leaves when the work unit functions shall not be unduly
         interrupted by the requesting officer’s absence.
C. Whenever an employee uses any accumulated holiday or compensatory leave, they shall
    complete their timesheet reflecting the use of this leave. If the use is via a call-off, the
    supervisor shall complete the timesheet on the employee’s behalf and provide notification of
    the entry to the employee.


           421.00        EMPLOYEE WELLNESS, RESILIENCY, AND
                               INTERVENTION

The Fort Worth Police Department recognizes that the overall wellness and resiliency of an
employee has an effect on both their work and home life. This General Order is intended to address
those aspects of the employee’s wellness as it relates to their work within the Police Department
and to establish various resources that are available to employees to promote their wellness and
resiliency. In addition, the Fort Worth Police Department employs an Early Intervention system
that is designed to facilitate an intervention process that objectively and analytically identifies
employees who may be in need and provides the employee with mentoring, training, or counseling.

421.01 WELLNESS UNIT
A. The Wellness Unit creates a culture that promotes and embraces employee wellness by
     providing all Fort Worth Police Department employees with training, support, and resources
     that promote a holistic approach to wellness benefiting both the employee and their families.
     This will be accomplished by providing education, access to resources, spousal/family
     support, and post-incident follow-ups through the check-point program.
B. The Wellness Unit is overseen by a Sergeant who supervises the Wellness Unit Corporal and
     officer(s), Physical Fitness Coordinator, and Peer Support Coordinator.
C. Wellness Unit personnel are on 24/7 emergency callback status and shall respond to all:
     1. Critical Police Events,
     2. Significant Events, or
     3. Any request from a field supervisor with the approval of the Wellness Unit Sergeant.
D. Check-Point Program
Check-point personnel are volunteer members selected from various divisions throughout the
department that receive specialized training from the Wellness Unit. Check-Point personnel will
contact employees who have experienced critical incidents, traumatic events, or hardships.
Personnel will provide support, and when appropriate, direct employees to the Wellness Unit for
referral for professional services. Methods of initiating a Check-Point contact may include:
                                           324
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


    1.   Police Communications Division notification of minor and major level incidents,
    2.   Requests from a peer or supervisor to check on a particular employee or group of
         employees, or
    3.   Notifications of injuries made by the Medical Records Unit.

421.02 PEER SUPPORT TEAM
A. Peer Support Team
    Peer Support personnel are beneficial to coworkers because they come from their homogenous
    group; therefore, giving them an “ethos” (credibility) that no academic training program can
    create. Peer Support members are not counselors or therapists, but are specially-trained
    colleagues who volunteer their time to provide intervention and assistance to police
    department employees involved in traumatic incidents and in times of personal and/or
    professional crisis. Since performing their duties as a Peer Support member is voluntary, Peer
    Support members shall not be additionally compensated by the Department for duties while
    serving as a Peer Support member, except as noted in General Order 421.02 B.
    1. The Peer Support Team is supervised by the Peer Support Coordinator who is appointed
         by the Chief of Police based on qualifications and training to further the mission of the
         Peer Support Team.
         a. When employees are directed to seek assistance from the Peer Support Coordinator
              or the Employee Assistance Program (EAP), only the supervisor or command staff
              with the need to know may be informed of the employee’s compliance with the
              directive. No other information or details shall be provided without the employee’s
              knowledge and permission.
         b. Conversations with Peer Support members are not protected by legal privilege
              however, communication with Peer Support members and employees are
              confidential through Police Department mandated policy, and in accordance with
              Texas Health and Safety Code, Chapter 784. Therefore, these conversations shall not
              be subject to any administrative investigation. The exceptions to confidentiality
              occur in cases where state or federal law requires divulgence, (similar to any
              physician, therapist or counselor):
              (1) A danger to self or others
              (2) Suspected child abuse
              (3) Narcotics offenses
              (4) Domestic violence
              (5) Factual elderly abuse, or
              (6) Felonies and serious misdemeanors.
    NOTE: If the Texas Health and Safety Code, Chapter 784 ever conflicts with this General
              Order, Chapter 784 will prevail.
B. Critical Incident Stress Management (CISM) Team
   CISM is a comprehensive, systematic and multicomponent approach for the reduction and
   mitigation of the harmful aspects of traumatic stress in the aftermath of major incidents,
   disasters, or catastrophes. Due to the advent of the Incident Command System and the National
   Incident Management System, the Fort Worth Police Department may find it necessary to send
   assistance to local, regional, or national agencies who request assistance. CISM is one of the
   services regularly requested, therefore, standardized training is necessary and expected.



                                          325
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


   1. The Peer Support Coordinator shall obtain the necessary training from the International
       Critical Incident Stress Foundation (ICISF) and will ensure the Peer Support members
       receive basic CISM training as well.
    2. The Peer Support Coordinator, or designee, will determine if CISM components should be
       employed following a critical or significant incident.
    3. The Peer Support Coordinator shall be contacted by a Police Communications Division
       Supervisor when a patrol supervisor has requested the services of the Peer Support Team.
    4. Notification of a Peer Support member shall be initiated by the Peer Support Coordinator
       directly or through the Police Communications supervisor. On-duty Peer Support members
       shall be given priority in selection due to the importance associated with rapid response;
       however, officers or employees may specifically request any peer support team member
       on the active list.
    5. With the permission of the investigator, Peer Support members may be allowed to
       accompany the employee through all phases of an investigation if requested by the
       concerned employee. The Peer Support member status is not official and they shall take
       no part in the investigation. Under no circumstances shall the Peer Support member do
       anything that might disrupt or interfere with the investigation. The Peer Support
       Coordinator shall be responsible for the supervision of the Peer Support member working
       with the concerned employee during the initial phases of their contact.
    6. Peer Support members shall not be used for regular police duties when off duty or acting
       in their capacity as a Peer Support member.
    7. In accordance with General Order 421.02 A., a Peer Support members shall maintain
       confidentiality for all conversations they are a party to between sworn officers and/or
       employees when performing peer support and/or CISM duties. Any breach of
       confidentiality, outside of what is required by law, shall subject the Peer Support member
       to disciplinary action and expulsion from the Peer Support Team.

421.03 CRISIS INTERVENTION TEAM
A. The department recognizes that each individual officer is valuable and that they are owed the
    appropriate care, attention, and resources that they need to overcome the challenges they are
    faced with in the profession of law enforcement. Encompassed within the mission of the Crisis
    Intervention Team (CIT) is safeguarding the welfare of our officers while maintaining their
    dignity, reputation, respect, and privacy. Whenever an officer or employee is experiencing a
    behavioral health crisis, the Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) shall respond to provide Critical
    Incident Stress Management Services and to support the welfare of the officer/employee and
    their families by referring them to available resources that will assist them in overcoming the
    challenges and stressors that led to the behavioral health crisis.
B. Confidentiality - All information related to services provided to officers shall be maintained
    as confidential pursuant to Texas Health and Safety Code Sec 784.001.
C. Definitions - Within the context of internal mental health, the following definitions apply
    under Texas Health and Safety Code Sec 784.001:
    1. The Crisis Intervention Team is a “Crisis Response Service.”
    2. Members of the Crisis Intervention Team are “Emergency Response Team Members.”
    3. The actions of the Crisis Intervention Team members are “Critical Incident Stress
         Management Services.”



                                           326
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


D. Officer Behavioral Health Crisis Signs:
   1. Signs of an officer behavioral health concern may include: Any indicators that an officer
       is in need of immediate intervention to protect the safety and wellbeing of themselves and
       others.
       a. Upon the receipt of information that an officer is experiencing a Behavioral Health
             Crisis, any officer or supervisor shall immediately notify the CIT Lieutenant during
             business hours or an on-call CIT supervisor after hours.
   NOTE: Notification to CIT should be made regardless of the status of the officer’s physical
             health (e.g., medication, intoxication, head injury, etc.)

421.04 VOLUNTEER CHAPLAINS
A. The police lead chaplain shall be appointed by the Chief of Police and is organizationally
    attached to the office of the Assistant Chief over the Finance and Personnel Bureau. The
    mission of the volunteer chaplain program is to provide non-denominational spiritual
    guidance, counseling and crisis intervention to the employees of the Fort Worth Police
    Department. Police Chaplain(s) shall demonstrate sensitivity to and respect for cultural,
    religion, gender, sexual orientation and physical differences when working with employees
    and the public.
    1. The police lead chaplain shall maintain a list of representative faiths and seek to recruit
         clergy members from those faiths to assist in the responsibilities of the police department
         as needed.
    2. The police lead chaplain shall be responsible for supervision, direction, and coordination
         with team police chaplains and, with assistance from the appropriate division(s), is
         responsible for background screening of team members, including but not limited to,
         criminal history checks, reference check, and degree and employment verification.
B. The police chaplain(s) shall be aware of the unique responsibilities of sworn and non-sworn
    employees.
    1. The police chaplain(s) will be available to all police personnel and their family members.
         Because of the confidential nature of the relationship, employees are not required to notify
         their supervisor of the consultation; however, the officer shall call off if the consultation
         will cause them to miss work.
         a. An employee's discussion with the chaplain concerning an addiction issue does not
              equate to self-referral. Refer to the City of Fort Worth Personnel Rules and
              Regulations, Alcohol Misuse and Drug Abuse Policy, for information related to self-
              referral.
    2. To the extent allowed by law, any communication that a person makes to a police chaplain
         is on strictly confidential basis and shall not be released to any party other than the person
         being counseled. Records and files shall be provided the utmost security.
    3. The police chaplain may be contacted either through Police Communications or directly
         by cell phone at any time.
C. The police chaplain(s) may not transport any person in their personal vehicle while on-duty
    with the police department.
D. The police chaplain(s) may ride-in with the officers to observe police operations and be on
    call to assist in situations where counseling or advice may be beneficial.
    1. Police chaplain(s) shall not interfere with any investigation or divulge information to
         family members, witnesses or victims without an approval from an on-duty supervisor.

                                            327
Fort Worth Police Department General Orders


    2. Police chaplain(s) shall refer all news media requests to the on-scene police supervisor or
       the Public Relations Office.
   3. Police chaplain(s) shall complete and sign a waiver which shall be kept on file with the
       Patrol Bureau office. Once the waiver has been completed and filed, the member will not
       be required to complete the waiver or have a criminal history check for each ride-in.
E. The police chaplain shall be notified immediately by Police Communications of an employee's
   on-duty death or serious injury.
   1. If requested by the department or the family, the lead police chaplain will assist in
       coordination of funeral or memorial services for in-the-line of duty deaths, and upon
       approval by the Assistant Chief may assist with the funeral or memorial services of any
       police employee.
   2. If requested by the department or employee, the police chaplain(s) will be available for
       visitation of a hospitalized or home-bound employee.
F. Police Chaplains(s) serve at the pleasure of the Chief of Police.

421.05 EARLY INTERVENTION
A. Purpose:
    1. Early Intervention (EI) is a multifaceted program designed to identify employees who
         may be facing professional or personal difficulties that are impacting their work
         performance and who may need some form of support, guidance, or assistance. The
         overall objective is to identify and mitigate behavior that may lead to performance issues,
         policy violations, and/or negatively impact employee wellness or community
         interactions.
    2. Early Intervention is separate from the disciplinary process and shall not be used as an
